Classes per word rise from 0.15 at step 1000 to 3.53 at 16000 and 5.88 at the final model (words with two or more: 0.02 to 0.46 to 0.71); among the words that have a class at all the count still rises, 1.26 to 5.32 to 6.90, so the rise is not only the words' classes growing past the half-cluster threshold. At 16000 a third of the words (0.34) are over the floor at half of no cluster (their classes are finer than the clusters) and 0.46 of clusters have two rows or more. - e596 THE MAGNITUDE BIAS (the MLP writes' exact coefficients at GPT-2 small block 6 and Pythia-410m block 12; the state decomposed over the full native dictionary at K = 64; identified writes scored as in the paper, and all selected MLP atoms; four solvers and the oracle support):

  | model, block | MLP writes' share of the state's energy | identified writes (selected atoms among the true top-64 / top-16 MLP writers) | relative error, median | sign accuracy | ratio estimate/truth, smallest / largest decile | all selected MLP atoms, smallest-decile ratio: OMP-64 / K = 128 truncated / sign-constrained / shrunk | oracle support: smallest / largest decile (relative error) | share of the true top-64 in the support |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | GPT-2 small, block 6 | 0.39 | 16233 / 9271 | 0.800 / 0.585 | 0.9919 / 0.9959 | 2.59 / 1.40 | 537.30 / 552.06 / 537.31 / 503.02 | 1.01 / 1.04 (0.632) | 0.12 |
  | Pythia-410m, block 12 | 0.25 | 7049 / 4813 | 0.996 / 0.753 | 0.9936 / 0.9956 | 2.88 / 1.18 | 867.15 / 847.57 / 867.16 / 750.38 | 0.85 / 0.65 (0.717) | 0.05 |

  - The paper's estimation picture reproduces in kind, and no refit removes the bias, because the bias is the support's. On identified writes the sign is right in 0.9919 / 0.9936 of cases and the magnitude is biased upward for small writes (2.59 / 2.88 at the smallest decile against 1.40 / 1.18 at the largest); the relative errors here (0.800 / 0.996) exceed the paper's 0.25-0.54 because the MLP-only truth used here leaves the attention writes, which carry most of these states' energy (the MLP writes carry 0.39 / 0.25), to be absorbed by the MLP support. Truncating a K = 128 support, constraining the sign and shrinking by the explained share change nothing; the oracle support alone removes the bias at GPT-2 (1.01 / 1.04) and reverses it at Pythia (0.85 / 0.65). The support beyond the largest writes is spurious, as the paper said: over all selected MLP atoms the smallest decile is estimated at 537 / 867 times its truth.
  - Pre-registered: B1 (truncation halves the bias) refuted; B2 (the oracle support still biased upward) refuted at GPT-2; B3 (the sign constraint changes nothing) confirmed.

  What the six answered: recruitment is a symptom of the class's geometry and not a performance event (the class learns at its tokens' pace, and the direction's effect is what it will be before the row arrives); unlearning leaves the writers untouched and silences half of them at the forgotten classes, and the share still writing tracks how fast the forgetting is undone; pruning helps grokking regardless of what is pruned, and S cannot guide it before generalisation; twins do not anchor a stitch; polysemanticity rises through training at any grain; and the instrument's bias is the support's, not the refit's. Four of the six were nulls, and each closes a door the paper's next reader would have opened.

SESSION 111 (a fresh box; the user: think it through, run the experiments, step into the shoes of the people who would use the unlearning audit, and look for what else is uncharted. The audit of session 110 tested as an unlearning researcher, a reviewer, a safety team and a continual-learning person would test it: five methods, two domains, two model sizes, a probe baseline, three recovery attacks; then the mirror question, where fine-tuning lives; then whether WDD can do the unlearning itself. Some thirty jobs.)

  - What the methods do to the writers, read on three levels. The rows: every training method leaves them untouched (cosine 0.9991 to 1.0000 across ascent, difference, NPO and RMU; change 0.81 to 1.29 times rows of the same norm), and only selective dampening reaches them (cosine 0.8585 to 0.9405, 2.27 to 12.68 times rows of the same norm), at a retain cost of +0.684 to +2.646. The writers' activation at the forgotten contexts: RMU never touches it (1.00 of the original in all 9 conditions), because it pushes the block-B state away from the writers downstream of them; ascent, difference and NPO silence the writers on Pythia-160m's PubMed (0.53 to 0.82 at +1 to +4 nats) but not on Github (0.95 to 0.99) nor on Pythia-410m (0.90 to 0.99), where they raise the loss through the readers instead; dampening silences them (-0.02 to 0.31). The state's projection on the writers falls under every method (still writing 0.03 to 0.54 for RMU, which also damages the retain words' writing, 0.22 to 0.74 from 1.00, with the retain loss almost unchanged, +0.028 to +0.907).
  - Depth is read on the parameter side, not the state side. Twenty relearning steps recover 0.83 to 0.96 of RMU's rise, 0.78 to 0.97 of ascent's, difference's and NPO's where they leave the writers firing, 0.56 to 0.83 where they silence them, and 0.38 to 0.49 of dampening's. Across the 39 training-method conditions the writers' activation ratio has the largest rank correlation with the recovery, 0.82 (Pythia-160m alone 0.85, Pythia-410m alone 0.72, without dampening 0.70); the state-side still-writing share of session 110 correlates at 0.39 overall and -0.68 on Pythia-410m, the probe at 0.67 and -0.03, because RMU drives both to their "forgotten" reading while being the shallowest. Session 110's number was right within one method on one model and wrong across methods and at the larger scale; the number that survives is whether the named writers still fire, with the rows' own change as the sign of a method that reaches them.
  - The attacks. Benign relearning on the retain set alone recovers 0.36 / -0.21 / 0.26 of the rise for ascent, difference and RMU on PubMed (on Github the ascent conditions' forget loss moves the other way, -0.13, the retain windows there being 34 documents whose style the fine-tuning drifts toward). Quantisation to 4 bits in groups of 64 recovers nothing at this scale (0.20 / -0.12 / -0.40); the quantisation itself costs the original 2.069 nats on PubMed, more than the unlearning, so the known quantisation attack is not reproducible on a 160m model with round-to-nearest weights. 8-bit changes nothing (-0.00).
  - The probe a reviewer would propose does not grade depth: after one nat of gradient ascent on Pythia-160m's PubMed it classifies 0.10 of the forget positions as forget (from 0.98), after RMU at +2 still 0.87, and on Pythia-410m after ascent to +7 nats still 0.97; it reads the direction of the state's shift, not whether the writers are gone.
  - Scale: on Pythia-410m no training method silences the writers (ascent 0.96 to 0.99, NPO 0.90 to 0.94, RMU 1.00) and all relearn fast (recovery 0.76 to 0.96 excluding the drift control); the state-side readings invert there (still-writing against recovery -0.68) while the activation ratio holds (0.72).
  - Pre-registered: A1 (ascent, difference and NPO: rows at cosine 0.99, still writing under 0.6, activation halved at +2) refuted in its activation half on Pythia-160m PubMed (0.72 / 0.70 / 0.72) and in both halves on Github and Pythia-410m; A2 (dampening changes the rows by 1.5 times or more) confirmed; A3 (still-writing predicts recovery better than the probe) refuted (0.39 against 0.67; the activation ratio 0.82); A4 (4-bit quantisation recovers half for the training methods) refuted; A5 (benign relearning recovers a quarter for ascent, difference and NPO) confirmed.

  - Fine-tuning lives in the readers, not in new writers. The domain loss falls by 0.233 on Github and 0.178 on PubMed with all parameters; 25 / 29 rows enter the domain's 256 words, every one with its row at cosine 0.99 or more with the original (1.00 / 1.00): the entrants are recruited as they stand, by being fed differently, not rewritten. Attention-only fine-tuning, which cannot touch a row, gains 0.130 / 0.106 with 20 / 24 entrants; MLP-only 0.199 / 0.163. The control domain's words keep writing for 1.00 / 1.00 under full fine-tuning. Two earlier runs of this experiment, 300 steps at 2e-5 on windows cut from 29 Github documents and 200 steps at 1e-5 on one window from each of 96 documents, memorised their training windows (batch loss 1.30 to 0.07) and raised the held-out domain loss by two nats: a learning audit needs one pass over many documents, which is what this run does.
  - Pre-registered: L1 (twenty or more entrants, most rows unchanged) confirmed; L2 (attention-only reaches half the gain with fewer entrants) confirmed; L3 (control words keep writing at 0.9 under all three) confirmed.

  - The audit can name the writers; removing them does not unlearn. Zeroing the 60 PubMed writers raises the forget loss by +0.08 nats (retain +0.016; Github +0.11), as many random rows +0.00; the wider net of 156 rows +0.16. The coalition carries the classes, as e590 and e591b said. But the writers matter for the way back: zeroing them after capped ascent to +2 slows the relearning (back within 0.1 nats after 95 steps against 60 for ascent alone on PubMed, over 100 against 35 on Github; twenty-step recovery 0.60 against 0.63 and 0.89 against 0.94; the hybrid's retain cost +0.188 / +0.680). Removal alone does not unlearn, because the class is carried by the coalition; removal after silencing takes away the fastest route back, because the relearning would otherwise reopen the silenced writers first. The audit can direct the second step of an unlearning even though it cannot be the first.
  - Pre-registered: G1 (zeroing the writers costs under 0.3 nats) confirmed; G2 (the wider net under 1 nat) confirmed; G3 (the hybrid relearns like ascent alone, within 20 steps) refuted, the hybrid relearns slower.

  What the session settled: the audit's right number is on the parameter side. Whether the named writers still fire at the forgotten contexts, and whether their rows moved, separates the methods by depth: RMU overrides and is the shallowest, ascent and difference and NPO silence and relearn in tens of steps, dampening reaches the rows and relearns slowest at a retain cost. The state-side share of session 110 and the reviewer's probe read the state's shift, which every method produces, and rank RMU as the deepest when it is the shallowest. Fine-tuning recruits existing rows by feeding them differently. Removing the rows the audit names does not unlearn on its own, because the coalition carries the classes, but removing them after a silencing method slows the relearning: the audit cannot be the first step of an unlearning and can direct the second.

SESSION 112 (the user: run them all with robust controls and out-of-the-box thinking, and check the scripts often. Every script smoke-tested at toy size on the box before its full run; the baseline that could sink the audit, the causal test it pointed at, and three new audits: refusal, merging, compression.)

  - The dictionary picks different neurons from the activation statistics: the difference-selected set overlaps the WDD forget words by Jaccard 0.06 (magnitude-selected 0.00, ratio-selected 0.00); 0.18 of the difference-selected neurons are words at all. The naive sets respond to the methods differently: under capped ascent the difference-selected neurons collapse (-0.14 of their activation) where the WDD writers fall to 0.76, and under RMU neither moves (1.02 / 1.00); the random set stays at 0.99 / 1.00 / 1.12 under ascent, RMU and dampening.
  - Over the 54 training-method conditions the strongest single correlate of the 20-step recovery is the WDD writers at their classes (0.89); a rank correlation only means something for a set whose ratio moves, and the interquartile ranges across conditions are 0.39 for the WDD writers, 1.28 difference-selected, 0.79 ratio-selected, 0.09 magnitude-selected and 0.01 for the random set, whose ratio never leaves 1; the WDD writers at their classes are at 0.89, the difference-selected set at 0.83, the magnitude-selected at 0.56, the random set at -0.01, all neurons at -0.30, the still-writing share at 0.36 and the probe at 0.73. By model: WDD 0.90 / 0.78, difference-selected 0.83 / 0.72, ratio-selected 0.93 / 0.78; by domain (Pythia-160m) WDD 0.94 / 0.38 on PubMed / Github against difference-selected 0.91 / 0.85; without dampening WDD 0.83, difference-selected 0.85, ratio-selected 0.79. A naive selection predicts relearnability about as well: the audit's substance is that domain-selective neurons still fire, and the dictionary is one way to find them. Seeds: over the 16 Pythia-160m PubMed conditions run twice, the writers' activation ratio agrees between seeds at Spearman 0.98 (median absolute difference 0.02) and the recovery at 0.98.
  - Pre-registered: N1 (difference-selected overlaps the WDD words by 0.3 or less) confirmed; N2 (WDD correlates with the recovery at least 0.1 higher than difference-selected) refuted (+0.06); N3 (the random set within 0.9-1.1 under every method) refuted.

  - Silencing the named writers after an unlearning slows the relearning, robustly. After capped ascent, zeroing the writers' inputs adds 40 relearning steps at the median (slower in 1.00 of 6 runs; PubMed +30, +35, +35, Github +60, +45, +65) and zeroing their write columns 40; after RMU the three Github runs are censored, RMU alone not being back within 100 steps there, and on the three PubMed runs silencing adds +50, +70, +55 steps (rows zeroed +50, +70, +55). As many random rows zeroed add 0 after ascent and 5 after RMU (per run +0, +0, +0, +15, +10, +0; +0, +5, +5). The difference-selected neurons silenced instead of the writers add 25 after ascent (Github +60, +45, +65, PubMed +5, +0, +0) and after RMU on PubMed +50, +25, +55: the selection matters on one domain and not the other. Silencing the writers alone, with no unlearning, raises the forget loss by +0.08 nats and is back within 0.1 after 5 steps: the writers are not where the knowledge is, and removing them after the unlearning removes the fastest route back.
  - Pre-registered: S1 (input silencing adds 30 after RMU and 20 after ascent) confirmed; S2 (the difference-selected set adds less than the WDD writers after RMU) confirmed; S3 (random rows add fewer than 10) confirmed.

- e604 THE REFUSAL AUDIT (Qwen2.5-0.5B base and instruct, block 12 of 24; 200 harmful requests from AdvBench and 200 Alpaca instructions in the chat template; words on the last eight positions of each prompt: 53 harmful-class and 32 harmless-class words of 256; refusal by phrase on greedy 32-token completions; two prefix jailbreaks; one epoch of benign Alpaca fine-tuning):

  | condition | refusal on harmful | on harmless | harmful-class writers' activation ratio | halved for | still writing | harmless-class still writing | probe reads harmful |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | the instruct model as is | 0.93 | 0.06 | 1.00 | | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.98 |
  | jailbreak: persona | 0.96 | 0.08 | 0.97 | 0.09 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 0.99 |
  | jailbreak: direct | 0.93 | 0.05 | 0.98 | 0.13 | 0.72 | 0.69 | 0.97 |
  | benign fine-tuning (one epoch of Alpaca) | 0.37 | 0.01 | 0.96 | 0.25 | 0.79 | 0.72 | 0.72 |

  - Where safety training put refusal: not in the rows. The harmful-class words' rows are at cosine 0.9973 with the base model's (all rows 0.9972, harmless-class words 0.9977); their neurons fire at the harmful prompts at 0.49 of the instruct model's level in the base model, and 0.34 of them are words on the base model's states (0.36 still write at their classes there; harmless-class words 0.41). Safety training recruited existing writers by feeding them more, as the learning audit found for domains; the base model refuses 0.04 of the harmful prompts, the instruct model 0.93.
  - Jailbreaks and benign fine-tuning: neither prefix jailbreak moves this model's refusal rate (0.96 / 0.93 from 0.93), and the writers fire as before under them (0.97 / 0.98); one epoch of benign Alpaca fine-tuning takes the refusal rate from 0.93 to 0.37 (harmless prompts 0.01), the known erosion, with the harmful-class writers at 0.96 of their activation (halved for 0.25), their rows at cosine 1.0000, and 0.79 still writing at their classes; the probe's reading of the prompts as harmful falls from 0.98 to 0.72. Where the refusal falls, the writers that fire on harmful requests keep firing: benign fine-tuning changes what is downstream of them, the override pattern the unlearning audit saw under RMU.
  - Pre-registered: R1 (rows at cosine 0.99 with the base, half of the words are words in the base) refuted; R2 (a jailbreak that halves refusal leaves the writers at 0.8) untestable, neither prefix moved the refusal rate on this model; R3 (benign fine-tuning that lowers refusal leaves the writers at 0.8) confirmed.

- e605 THE MERGING AUDIT (Pythia-160m fine-tuned on Github and on PubMed for one epoch each; the two merged by averaging, or added in full; each alone; one at half strength; sequential Github-then-PubMed; the entrants of each fine-tune (22 Github, 31 PubMed; Jaccard between them 0.02, between the fine-tuned word sets 0.17, original 0.18) followed into each model):

  | model | Github loss | PubMed loss | control loss | Github entrants still writing (words) | PubMed entrants still writing (words) | original Github words writing | original PubMed words writing |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | the original | 1.228 | 2.739 | 3.050 | | | 1.00 | 1.00 |
  | github_ft | 1.000 | 2.982 | 3.282 | 1.00 (1.00) | 0.83 (0.32) | 0.99 | 1.00 |
  | pubmed_ft | 1.392 | 2.575 | 3.324 | 0.88 (0.45) | 1.00 (1.00) | 0.99 | 0.99 |
  | merged | 1.102 | 2.652 | 3.196 | 1.00 (0.50) | 0.90 (0.55) | 0.99 | 1.00 |
  | merged_full | 1.186 | 2.837 | 3.643 | 0.94 (0.59) | 1.00 (0.71) | 0.96 | 0.98 |
  | github_half | 1.055 | 2.785 | 3.097 | 0.94 (0.41) | 0.80 (0.26) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
  | sequential_github_then_pubmed | 1.138 | 2.582 | 3.403 | 1.00 (0.50) | 1.00 (0.65) | 0.96 | 0.99 |

  - The two fine-tunes recruit different rows (Jaccard 0.02 between their entrants; the fine-tuned word sets overlap by 0.17, the original's by 0.18), and the averaged model keeps about half of each fine-tune's gain (1.102 on Github against 1.000 fine-tuned and 1.228 original; 2.652 on PubMed against 2.575 and 2.739) at a control cost of +0.146. The still-writing share is lenient for entrants, since their rows already wrote at those positions before being promoted into the 256 (the Github entrants still write at 0.88 in the PubMed fine-tune, which never saw Github); the stricter count, the share of entrants that remain words, is 0.50 / 0.55 in the averaged model, 0.50 / 0.65 after sequential fine-tuning, 0.45 for the Github entrants in the PubMed fine-tune alone, and 0.41 at half strength. Sequential fine-tuning keeps more of the first domain's gain than expected (1.138 on Github), so at one epoch each there is little for merging to rescue.
  - Pre-registered: M1 (entrants overlap by 0.2 or less) confirmed; M2 (merging keeps 0.6 of each fine-tune's entrants where sequence keeps 0.3 or less of Github's) refuted, sequence keeps them too (1.00); M3 (the merged losses within 0.1 of the fine-tunes') refuted.

- e606 THE COMPRESSION AUDIT (Pythia-410m block 12, six Pile domains with 256 words and domain words pubmed 5, github 10, wikipedia 9, stackexchange 13, freelaw 13, uspto 9; 8-bit per channel, 4-bit in groups of 64 and 32, 3-bit in groups of 64, magnitude pruning of 30% and 50%; per-domain loss damage against the domain's writers' activation ratio and silenced share):

  | compression | pubmed: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | github: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | wikipedia: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | stackexchange: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | freelaw: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | uspto: damage / writers' activation / silenced share | random rows' activation | Spearman damage vs activation within |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | int8_per_channel | +0.002 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.002 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.002 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.003 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.003 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.003 / 1.01 / 0.00 | 1.00 | 0.03 |
  | int4_g64 | +0.379 / 0.91 / 0.00 | +0.345 / 0.99 / 0.00 | +0.363 / 0.94 / 0.00 | +0.300 / 0.92 / 0.15 | +0.434 / 0.90 / 0.00 | +0.306 / 0.98 / 0.11 | 0.98 | -0.60 |
  | int4_g32 | +0.300 / 1.00 / 0.00 | +0.311 / 1.02 / 0.00 | +0.293 / 0.96 / 0.00 | +0.259 / 0.92 / 0.08 | +0.347 / 0.95 / 0.00 | +0.227 / 0.99 / 0.00 | 1.00 | 0.20 |
  | int3_g64 | +2.195 / 0.43 / 1.00 | +2.796 / 0.59 / 0.70 | +1.973 / 0.53 / 0.78 | +1.951 / 0.63 / 0.69 | +2.900 / 0.59 / 0.85 | +1.773 / 0.59 / 0.67 | 1.02 | -0.43 |
  | prune30 | +0.866 / 0.61 / 1.00 | +1.057 / 0.83 / 0.10 | +0.833 / 0.81 / 0.44 | +0.824 / 0.75 / 0.62 | +1.416 / 0.77 / 0.54 | +0.708 / 0.73 / 0.67 | 1.09 | 0.43 |
  | prune50 | +4.160 / -0.02 / 1.00 | +4.534 / 0.11 / 0.80 | +3.771 / 0.08 / 0.89 | +3.623 / 0.14 / 0.77 | +4.757 / 0.13 / 1.00 | +3.700 / 0.29 / 0.67 | 1.30 | -0.43 |

  - Across compressions the damage and the silencing rise together (Spearman -0.94 between a domain's damage and its writers' activation ratio over 36 compression-by-domain pairs; with the share silenced 0.82), but most of that is severity: a harsher compression both damages every domain more and silences every domain's writers more, and the random rows' activation ratio (1.00, 0.98, 1.00, 1.02, 1.09, 1.30 across the six compressions) shows that only 3-bit and pruning touch neurons at all. The question the audit would have to answer is which domain a given compression hurts, and within single compressions the six-domain correlation is int8_per_channel 0.03, int4_g64 -0.60, int4_g32 0.20, int3_g64 -0.43, prune30 0.43, prune50 -0.43: inconsistent at this size, with five to thirteen domain words per domain. Pruning half the weights silences 0.85 of the writers at the median domain and costs +4.091 nats; 3-bit quantisation 0.78 and +2.265; 4-bit in groups of 64 0.04 and +0.355, in groups of 32 0.01 and +0.290; 8-bit nothing.
  - Pre-registered: C1 (damage correlates with the writers' activation at -0.5 or beyond) confirmed across compressions, where severity carries it; not within; C2 (4-bit in groups of 64 silences fewer than a fifth of any domain's writers) confirmed; C3 (pruning at 50% silences more and damages more than 3-bit) confirmed.

  What the session settled: the audit's substance is that domain-selective neurons still fire, and the dictionary is one of several ways to find them; silencing the named writers after an override method buys relearning resistance; safety training, like domain fine-tuning, recruits existing writers by feeding them more and leaves their rows alone, and benign fine-tuning erodes refusal with those writers still firing, an override downstream of them (the two prefix jailbreaks did not move this model); merged fine-tunes keep both sets of recruits because they recruit different rows; and compression damage tracks the silencing of writers across compressions through their severity, not within one compression across domains.

SESSION 113 (a fresh box, 2026-10-08; the user: do your magic. Four directions left open by session 112, every script smoke-tested before its full run: the refusal direction and its writers, writer rescue, the causal test at 410m with the activation trajectory, and the baseline at 1B.)

- e607 THE REFUSAL DIRECTION AND ITS WRITERS (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and 1.5B-Instruct; the difference-of-means direction between harmful and harmless prompts at the last prompt position, taken at the block among B-4, B, B+4 whose ablation at every block lowers refusal most; the harmful-class words as e604; the writers' rows' cosine with the direction, their share of the MLP writes' mass along it at the last position, their activation under ablation, and refusal induced by adding the direction):

  | model | blocks | harmful-class words | refusal harmful / harmless | direction block (of B-4, B, B+4) | ablated: refusal harmful / harmless | writers' rows absolute cosine with the direction / harmless-class / all rows | the most aligned rows that are words | writers' share of the MLP mass along it (most aligned rows / random) | writers' activation under ablation (halved for) | still writing | probe | direction added: refusal on harmless (from) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | 24 | 53 | 0.93 / 0.06 | 16 | 0.04 / 0.03 | 0.034 / 0.026 / 0.024 | 0.04 | 0.11 (0.22 / -0.01) | 0.99 (0.09) | 0.92 | 0.96 | 0.88 (0.06) |
  | Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | 28 | 59 | 0.99 / 0.07 | 14 | 0.03 / 0.01 | 0.026 / 0.033 / 0.023 | 0.14 | 0.01 (-0.10 / -0.00) | 0.88 (0.24) | 0.61 | 0.00 | 0.98 (0.07) |

  - The refusal direction exists and does its job, and the harmful-request writers do not write it. Ablating the direction at every block takes refusal on harmful prompts from 0.93 to 0.04 on the 0.5B model and from 0.99 to 0.03 on the 1.5B (the harmless rate 0.03 / 0.01); adding it to harmless prompts induces refusal at 0.88 / 0.98. The harmful-class writers' rows have a median absolute cosine of 0.034 / 0.026 with the direction against 0.024 / 0.023 for all rows, and of the rows most aligned with it only 0.04 / 0.14 are words at all; the writers carry 0.11 / 0.01 of the MLP writes' mass along the direction at the last position (the most aligned rows 0.22 / -0.10, random rows -0.01 / -0.00). Under the ablation the writers fire at 0.99 / 0.88 of their activation and 0.92 / 0.61 still write at their classes; the probe reads the prompts as harmful at 0.96 / 0.00. The writers that fire on harmful requests mark the request; the refusal is carried by a direction they do not write, and removing it, like benign fine-tuning (e604), overrides downstream of them.
  - Pre-registered: D1 (ablation halves refusal) confirmed; D2 (the writers' rows align with the direction at twice the all-rows cosine and carry a quarter of its mass) refuted; D3 (the writers keep firing at 0.8 under ablation) confirmed.

Silencing the writers after capped ascent adds 10 relearning steps at the median (slower in 1.00 of 3 seeds; per seed +10, +5, +10), zeroing their write columns 10 (+10, +5, +10), against 0 for as many random rows (+5, +0, +0) and 5 for the difference-selected neurons (+10, +5, +5); after RMU the writers add 5 (+5, +15, +5) and random rows 5 (+5, +5, +0), indistinguishable. At 160m the same silencing added 40 steps after ascent and 50 to 70 after RMU (e603); at 410m the three seeds agree on the direction after ascent and on little else. The writers are a smaller share of the rows at 410m (64 of 53,248 against 60 of 21,504) and the relearning has more paths around them. The trajectory: through the ascent the writers' activation stays between 0.94 and 0.99 in every seed while the forget loss climbs from 2.62 to 5.30 by step 85; under RMU it stays at 1.00 throughout. Silencing alone, with no unlearning, raises the forget loss by +0.02 nats and is back within 0.1 after 5 steps.
  - Pre-registered: T1 (input silencing after ascent adds 30 or more at 410m) refuted; T2 (the writers stay above 0.9 through the ascent trajectory) confirmed (minimum 0.94); T3 (random rows add fewer than 10) confirmed.

Restoring the WDD writers' activations after capped ascent recovers 0.09 of the rise on Pythia-160m PubMed, -0.01 on Github and 0.01 on Pythia-410m (after NPO 0.10 / 0.00 / 0.05); restoring every MLP neuron of blocks 0-B recovers 0.02 / 0.26 / -0.20 after ascent, so what the gradient methods change is not the MLP activations of those blocks at all but the attention and the later blocks, and the writers' silencing (e597: activation 0.70 here on PubMed) is a symptom of that change, not its carrier. After RMU restoring every MLP neuron of blocks 0-B recovers 0.75 / 0.57 / 0.83, since RMU's change is in the rows of blocks B-2..B that read those activations, while restoring the writers alone recovers 0.04 / -0.00 / 0.00. The reverse patch, the original model given the unlearned writers' activations, costs it 0.02 of the rise after ascent (every MLP neuron 0.15). Together with e603 and e608: silencing the writers does not forget and restoring them does not remember, yet removing them after an unlearning slows the relearning, because they are the fastest path the relearning would rebuild.

SESSION 114 (2026-10-08, box 8; the user: do whatever feels right. The two experiments the J-Lens post pointed at (Gurnee et al. 2026; the J++ Lens): the word's class as the free expert partition for a transported write, and the refusal question of e607 re-asked with transport.)

- e611 CLASS-CONDITIONED DESCENDANTS (Pythia-410m, blocks 4, 8, 12; for the 40 words with the largest classes at each block, four predictions of the output change the word's write makes, compared as directions in logit space with the actual change when a held-out class position alone is perturbed by the row: the raw row through the unembedding, the row transported by the Jacobian averaged over every position at once, over a random subset of positions of the class's size, and over the training half of the class):

  | block | words | cosine with the actual logit change at held-out class positions: raw row | global map | random-subset map | class map | class beats global / beats the random subset (share of words) | top-10 overlap: raw / global / random subset / class | at positions outside the class: raw / global / random subset / class |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 4 | 40 | 0.065 | 0.071 | 0.210 | 0.283 | 0.97 / 0.78 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.04 | 0.081 / 0.156 / 0.271 / 0.191 |
  | 8 | 40 | 0.089 | 0.141 | 0.284 | 0.423 | 1.00 / 0.90 | 0.01 / 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.04 | 0.112 / 0.193 / 0.340 / 0.212 |
  | 12 | 40 | 0.135 | 0.295 | 0.388 | 0.482 | 1.00 / 0.88 | 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.03 / 0.05 | 0.157 / 0.318 / 0.417 / 0.345 |

  - The class map is the faithful one, for two reasons of unequal size. Most of its lead over the all-positions map is the estimate: perturbing every position at once lets the perturbations interfere through attention, and a map averaged over a random subset of positions of the class's size already reaches 0.210 / 0.284 / 0.388 against the all-positions map's 0.071 / 0.141 / 0.295. The conditioning adds the rest: the class map reaches 0.283 / 0.423 / 0.482, +0.073 / +0.139 / +0.094 over the random subset, beating it for 0.78 / 0.90 / 0.88 of words. At block 4 the cosine between the predicted and the actual logit change is 0.065 for the raw row, 0.071 for the global map, 0.210 for a map averaged over a random subset of positions of the class's size, and 0.283 for the class map (the class map beats the global one for 0.97 of words and the random subset for 0.78); at block 12 0.135 / 0.295 / 0.388 / 0.482. The gap between the class map and the all-positions map does not close late (+0.212 at block 4, +0.186 at block 12), unlike the J++ experts, which agreed more in later layers; the conditioning gap is largest in the middle. At positions outside the class the class map reads 0.191 at block 4 and 0.345 at block 12 against the random-subset map's 0.271 and 0.417: the class map is a map of its class and a worse map of everything else, as the J++ experts are maps of their clusters. The top-10 tokens of the predicted and actual changes overlap by 0.04 to 0.05 even for the class map: the maps get the direction of a write's effect in logit space, not its specific tokens, at this perturbation size. The raw row, the logit lens of the write, is the worst at every block and near zero: what a row says through the unembedding is not what its write does.
  - Pre-registered: J1 (class beats global by 0.10 at block 4) confirmed (+0.212); J2 (the gap under 0.03 at block 12) refuted (+0.186); J3 (the raw row worst at every block) confirmed; J4 (the class map beats the random-subset map by 0.10 at block 4) refuted (+0.073; +0.139 at block 8, +0.094 at block 12).

The harmful-class writers' absolute cosine with the direction goes from 0.034 raw to 0.101 transported (harmless-class writers 0.083, the rows most aligned in the raw measure 0.203, random rows 0.103); their transported share of the projection on the direction at the last position is -0.05 (random rows -0.03). Silencing them on the input side leaves the projection at 0.88 of the original and the refusal rate at 0.89 (from 0.93); random rows 1.00 and 0.93, the harmless-class writers 1.01 and 0.95. e607's conclusion stands with a footnote: the writers feed a small part of the direction (the projection falls by 12 percent when they are silenced, by none when random rows are) and none of the refusal, which is carried by components they do not feed.

  What the session settled: a write's class is the partition the J++ Lens had to learn, and the class-conditioned map is the most faithful one, more by the estimate than by the conditioning; and the refusal question keeps its answer, with a small upstream share now measured, once the writers' rows are measured where they arrive rather than where they leave.

  - A rule, not just a correlation. For the recovery criterion the WDD writers' activation has an AUC of 0.93 and a leave-one-method-out accuracy of 0.89 against a majority baseline of 0.57, flagging the held-out method correctly at 0.93 / 0.67 / 0.80 / 1.00 / 1.00 for ascent / difference / NPO / RMU / dampening; the difference-selected set has the same AUC (0.94) but transfers worse (0.78), the ratio-selected set 0.83, the probe 0.84, the still-writing share 0.33, the forget rise 0.38. For the steps-back criterion every activation measure is weak (AUC 0.71 for the writers) and the forget rise is the best rule (0.81): how many steps a relearning needs is mostly how far the loss was raised, and what the audit predicts is the share of the rise a fixed budget recovers.

The prefix is a different document, so it raises the original's loss too (+0.08 on PubMed, +0.18 on Github at 160m); against that the in-context recovery is at 160m -0.03 / -0.67 after ascent, 0.02 / 0.01 after NPO, -0.02 / -0.12 after RMU; at 410m -0.21 / -0.67 after ascent, -0.01 / -0.66 after NPO, -0.04 / -0.22 after RMU; at 1B -0.06 / -1.39 after ascent, 0.08 / -0.98 after NPO, -0.13 / -0.37 after RMU (PubMed / Github). After ascent and RMU the forget-domain prefix deepens the suppression: at 160m on Github the unlearned model's forget loss rises by +1.12 after ascent and +0.44 after RMU against the original's +0.18; after NPO it moves with the original (+0.16); the largest deepening is +0.94 nats beyond the original's rise (160m, github, ascent). An off-domain prefix does the opposite: at 160m on Github the forget loss falls by -0.31 after ascent and -0.12 after RMU while the original's rises by +0.19, a recovery of 0.03 to 0.35 over the sizes. The suppression the methods learned is keyed to the context they trained in: more of that context, more suppression. The silenced writers do not wake in context: after ascent on PubMed at 160m they fire at 0.69 of their activation without context and 0.64 with it (NPO 0.73 to 0.68); after RMU they fire at 1.00 either way. Against this, on TOFU two forget pairs in the prompt recover 0.26 / 0.22 / 0.39 of the rise after ascent / NPO / RMU: the task, not the size, is what a prompt can reach.
  - Pre-registered for 160m: I1 (the forget-domain prefix recovers 0.4 of RMU's rise and 0.2 or less of ascent's) refuted; I2 (ascent's writers fire at 0.85 in context) refuted; I3 (the retain-domain prefix recovers less than half of what the forget-domain prefix recovers) refuted.

  What the session settled: as a rule the writers' activation transfers to unseen methods at 0.89 accuracy where its naive siblings reach 0.78 to 0.83 and the probe 0.84; on TOFU the forget set is not a domain in the dictionary's sense (2 of 256 words pass the forget threshold; the 32 most forget-leaning words average 0.62 forget share where a neutral word sits at 0.52) and the audit has nothing to read: the ranked writers fire at 0.99 to 1.00 after every method, so their 0.76 correlation with the recovery is the ordering of RMU's 1.00 against 0.99 and carries nothing; the auditors with signal there are the output KL (0.82) and the representation drift (0.76), which rank RMU (recovery 1.00 in 10 steps) above NPO (0.70) and ascent (0.57), while the membership AUC (-0.57) and the probe (-0.86) point the wrong way; and on the Pile no prompt undoes a weight change at 160m, 410m and 1B: a page of the forgotten domain (PubMed / Github) recovers at 160m -0.03 / -0.67 after ascent, 0.02 / 0.01 after NPO, -0.02 / -0.12 after RMU; at 410m -0.21 / -0.67 after ascent, -0.01 / -0.66 after NPO, -0.04 / -0.22 after RMU; at 1B -0.06 / -1.39 after ascent, 0.08 / -0.98 after NPO, -0.13 / -0.37 after RMU, deepening ascent's rise instead (up to +0.94 nats beyond the original's rise under the same page, 160m github), while an off-domain page recovers 0.03 to 0.35; on TOFU two forget pairs in the prompt recover 0.26 / 0.22 / 0.39 of the rise after ascent / NPO / RMU. The audit is a usable rule for the share of a forget rise a relearning recovers, conditional on the loss having risen, on forget sets that are domains; it is not a rule for how many steps the relearning takes, and it has nothing to read when the forget set shares its words with what is kept.

The rule does not survive the held-out domains at the fixed cut, nor the architecture; the writers add predictive value beyond the loss, the KL and the drift; and silencing them delays relearning no more than silencing the naive sets.

SESSION 118 (2026-10-09, box 8 and the laptop; the user: WDD is a new method, so it may be useless on existing problems and decisive on new ones; review the literature, re-read the program, evolve WDD at its core, and explore several candidate directions with quick experiments. Pre-registered D1 to D3, E1 to E3 and F1 to F3 at 2026-10-09 09:30:02, before the runs.)

  The re-reading (THEORY.md related work, sessions 101 to 110): what the native dictionary has that a learned one lacks is the parameter behind each direction, the row; everything state-side (which neurons fire, which direction a class is spoken along) a learned dictionary or a naive selector reaches as well. So the candidate directions are parameter-side: diffing two fine-tunes by row identity with no training, editing a concept in the weights through the one row that writes it, and training a model to be self-describing in its own rows. The literature (session 118 related work in THEORY.md) has crosscoder diffing with sparsity artefacts, neuron editing by selection among fifty to a hundred and fifty neurons, SAE tracking through training that cannot name the parameter, and codebook or sparse-by-design training with extra parameters; none has the row as the unit.

SESSION 123 (2026-10-09, box 8; the user: do the literature review, steelman the data-to-parameter experiment, and run the refined version. Pre-registered D1 to D4 at 2026-10-09 14:31:23, before the runs.)

  The literature (THEORY.md, session 123 related work): Mechanistic Data Attribution (Chen et al., ICML 2026, arXiv 2601.21996) traces interpretable attention heads to training samples by EK-FAC influence functions and shows, by retraining Pythia-14M to 160M inside a developmental window on the real data order, that deleting or adding a small fraction of high-influence samples delays or accelerates the emergence of induction heads, with random interventions doing nothing; MLP neurons are not among its units and SAE features get only qualitative examples. Symbolic MDA (arXiv 2606.29171) attributes a feature-built policy rather than a feature. So the data-to-unit intervention exists for heads; what the dictionary adds is an attribution that costs nothing (the class is the attribution, no influence computation) for a unit that is a weight row, and the test here is whether that free attribution is causal. The steelman against running it: the real run's recruitment between steps 8000 and 10000 took four billion tokens, and a continuation here is five million; e590 (session 109) found substitute speakers in 0.30 of classes within 2.5 million tokens at step 8000, which is the only reason to expect recruitment dynamics at this scale.

SESSION 124 (2026-10-09, no box; the user: a literature review of the results the program calls positive. No experiment; the review is [`REVIEW_POSITIVE_CLAIMS.md`](REVIEW_POSITIVE_CLAIMS.md).)

  Method: web searches on 2026-10-09 for each positive claim (single-unit grammatical and gender neurons; unlearning reversibility and its predictors; feature and neuron dynamics across Pythia checkpoints; forecasts of feature and circuit formation; extreme-value calibration of maximum projections; attention against MLP energy over training; cross-lingual concepts; substitution after neuron removal), two papers read in full (arXiv 2605.18789, 2412.17626), the rest from arXiv abstracts, and every paper cited from memory confirmed on its arXiv page.

  What the review found, claim by claim: the floor is standard extreme-value statistics (Donoho and Johnstone 1994; Cai and Jiang 2012); the row as a unit is the neuron literature's oldest unit (Lakretz 2019, Geva 2022, Dai 2022, Gurnee 2023, Voita 2023), so session 121's 'a unit the literature does not have' is withdrawn as worded; the developmental ordering, positions first and direction later, with early forecastability of persistence, is reported for sparse-autoencoder features across Pythia checkpoints by Stecher et al. (May 2026, arXiv 2605.18789, persistence predicted at AUC 0.80 / 0.83) and SAE-Track (Dec 2024, arXiv 2412.17626), both before the program's sessions, while the parameter's identity (the nearest row), its forecast at AUC 0.93, its gradient source and the loss-matched control are not found anywhere; replacement after removal is in Lo, Cohen and Barez 2024 (arXiv 2401.01814), where the program's own scale test (e590) found none within its budget; the unlearning audit's substance, that the activation side predicts reversibility where the loss and the weight distance do not, is in Xu et al. (ICML 2026, arXiv 2505.16831), Song et al. (Aug 2026, arXiv 2608.11408, 398 unlearned models), Goel et al. (EACL 2026) and the weight-space line (Siddiqui et al., NeurIPS 2025; its LLM follow-up arXiv 2608.25429), with the rows-unchanged reading, the leave-one-domain-out transfer with its +0.31 and the floor-artefact warning not found; the single-row gender dial and its cross-lingual effect are single-unit grammatical dials (Lakretz 2019; Vig 2020; Finlayson 2021), edited gender neurons (arXiv 2501.14457; You et al. 2026) and gender neurons shared across 43 languages in encoders (Stańczak et al. 2022), the program's locator being the ordinary contrast-activation selector, with only the weight-row sign flip at near-zero cost in three languages with placebo rows not found; programmable placement is concept whitening and concept bottlenecks (Chen, Bei and Rudin 2020; Koh et al. 2020) in another unit, and e627 had already narrowed it to the description.

  What changed in the record: GRAPH H593-H596 carry the verdicts; THEORY gets a session-124 related-work section; PAPER.md a prior-art section; RELATED_WORK.md a pointer; DIGEST's corrections bullet names the withdrawn sentence. The program's standing verdict (session 118) is unchanged: the deepest result is the recruitment law at the parameter level, the practical one the audit, and the dictionary is not essential downstream. The review narrows the first to its parameter-level parts and reclassifies the second as a replication with a transfer test.

SESSION 126 (2026-10-10, no box; the user: is any of this novel, do a thorough review, and the WDD paper never cited the paper that does the same decomposition with simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit on another architecture.   Found and read in full: Head Pursuit (Basile et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2510.21518) decomposes each attention head's residual-stream write by simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit onto the model's own unembedding rows, with no training, on Mistral-7B and three vision-language models: the same object as WDD with the read-out rows as the dictionary and heads as the thing decomposed, which the WDD paper did not cite; Arora et al. (ICML 2026, arXiv 2601.22594) establish that MLP neurons are as sparse a feature basis as autoencoders and trace circuits in the neuron basis, the strongest form of the row-as-unit claim; the nearest-row recruitment is predicted by small-initialisation theory (Maennel 2018; Boursier and Flammarion, JMLR; Chen et al. 2023; Min et al. 2024) and proved for autoencoder training with an alignment threshold of the floor's extreme-value form (Chen et al. 2025, arXiv 2506.14002, from an excerpt), and the read-write asymmetry e631 saw is Wang 2026 (arXiv 2608.06766); so the method is a variant of a published idea, the unit claim is better established elsewhere, and what remains the program's own is the measurement in language-model pretraining: which row of tens of thousands is recruited for a class present in the states, forecast two checkpoints ahead on five runs, which a learned dictionary's decoder cannot name. Also placed: SITH (CVPR 2026, coherent OMP of CLIP head singular vectors onto concept embeddings, data-free), ITDA, MP-SAE, ROTATE, ASPD, bilinear MLPs; the developmental feature trackers without a parameter (Ge et al. ICLR 2026 crosscoders; Jarve et al. CIKM 2026 feature migration across layers; Ranadive et al. 2023 early class-selective neurons).

  What the session settled: the method's ingredients are all in print and its nearest prior work was uncited; the surviving claim is a measurement of a predicted mechanism, not a discovery of it. The WDD paper's related work needs Head Pursuit and Arora et al.

SESSION 128 (2026-10-11, no box; the user: is the ticket at initialisation a nothingburger? The box was released before the direct test (e632b, the residual of the initial row orthogonal to its final direction, with a persistence-matched null; written, not run) could run; the answer comes from e632's own numbers.)

  The confound: a row keeps part of its initial direction, and a class's direction is correlated with its speaker's final direction because the speaker writes the class, so a random initial direction looks aligned with the class merely by surviving into the final row. Neither control of session 127 removes this: the own-write subtraction leaves the coalition, which co-adapts with the row, and the cross-seed speaker is still selected by its final direction. The arithmetic from the recorded numbers:

  | seed | persistence of the recruit's row (cosine with its step-0 row) at 1000 / 4000 / 16000 (all rows at 16000) | observed initial cosine with the class direction (rank) | final row's cosine with the class direction that persistence alone needs to give it | own write subtracted: direction's cosine with the final row, observed rank | persistence the path needs / measured | rank the path predicts from the measured persistence |

  - What this withdraws: session 127's reading that initialisation biases which row is recruited. What stands from e632: the recruits' rows rotate as far as any row (persistence 0.85 at step 1000, 0.3 at 4000, 0.13 at 16000), the step-0 rank does not set the recruitment time, and the identification figures of part C, which restate e587's geometry among the non-word rows against usage. The small-initialisation lottery is neither confirmed nor refuted in pretraining by this design; a test needs the residual component or a null that keeps each row's persistence, and it needs the vectors, which went with the box.

  What the session settled: the ticket at initialisation is the row's persistence and nothing more is shown; e632 is narrowed to its negative and descriptive parts.

  - The ring's radius relative to the state norm falls with depth, from 0.33 to 0.55 at the embedding to 0.10 to 0.27 at the last block before the final norm, while the cyclic order persists on the best block's plane through the later blocks in every model but Pythia-160m's months, which lose it after block 10.
  - Pre-registered: M1 (weekdays: at the best block the seven day means lie in a plane carrying 0.6 or more of their between-day variance, in full cyclic order (7 of 7 adjacencies), on Pythia-160m; a replication of Engels et al. 2024 in a new model) confirmed; M2 (the token embeddings alone already carry the cyclic order (6 or more of 7 adjacencies), so the ring is inherited from the embedding rather than built by the blocks) confirmed; M3 (the ring is diffuse: 100 or more MLP rows are needed to account for half of the MLP-written between-day pattern in the ring plane at the best block; there is no small native block) confirmed; M4 (phase coding: the twenty most day-selective rows per day write at phases aligned with that day's angle in the ring plane, mean cosine 0.5 or more (random rows give about 0)) refuted; M5 (transport: the ring persists in the plane fitted at the best block for at least three later blocks (6 or more adjacencies when later day means are projected onto that plane) while its radius relative to the state norm falls) confirmed; M6 (months: a ring at the best block with 10 or more of 12 adjacencies) confirmed; M7 (the MLP writes carry less than half of the ring's between-day pattern at the best block; the embedding and attention carry the rest) refuted; M8 (the same holds on GPT-2 small and Qwen2.5-0.5B for M1 and M6 (cyclic order present), with the best block in the first half of depth) refuted. M5 is judged on months, since the weekday ring's best block on Pythia-160m has fewer than three later blocks; M8 fails only on the position of GPT-2's best block, every block of GPT-2 having the full order.
  - Caveats: thirty templates per class; the top-2 share is not discriminative against shuffled labels (the shuffle null gives similar shares), so the order with its shuffle p-value is the test; the rows-for-half count uses signed attributions to the pattern; the ledger shares exclude the final-norm block.

  What the session settled: on six models the seven weekday means at the best block lie in cyclic order in a plane (7 of 7 adjacencies, shuffle p at most 0.01) and so do the twelve months (12 of 12), the replication of Engels et al. 2024; the token embeddings already carry the weekday order in all six models (7 of 7) and the month order in three; the blocks do not keep the embedding's ring but build a new one in a nearly orthogonal plane: the ring pattern's energy in the embedding's plane is 0.00 to 0.11 by block 2 and the best block's plane has principal cosines of at most 0.29 with it. the new ring is written by the MLP rows: their writes carry 0.69 to 1.00 of the weekday pattern and 0.80 to 1.02 of the month pattern at the best block, the rest attention; it is diffuse in most models (Pythia-160m 181, GPT-2 small 156, Qwen2.5-0.5B 68, Pythia-410m 394, SmolLM2-135M 130, OLMo-1B 28 rows for half of the weekday pattern; months 252, 182, 23, 522, 169, 4), with OLMo-1B's months carried half by 4 rows, the one small native block; the most day-selective rows write at the day's angle in four of the six models (phase coding Pythia-160m -0.04, GPT-2 small 0.36, Qwen2.5-0.5B 0.34, Pythia-410m -0.03, SmolLM2-135M 0.28, OLMo-1B 0.17 against random rows near zero), absent in both Pythias. the ring's radius relative to the state norm falls with depth, from 0.33 to 0.55 at the embedding to 0.10 to 0.27 at the last block before the final norm, while the cyclic order persists on the best block's plane through the later blocks in every model but Pythia-160m's months, which lose it after block 10. Reading: the calendar manifold is known; what is new and small is where it lives and who writes it: the embedding's ring is abandoned by block 2, the blocks rebuild one in a new plane, the MLP rows write it, diffusely in five models and in a handful of rows in one, and in four models the rows that select a day also point at it. A descriptive result with a null and six models, not a nothingburger and not a paper; the one claim it supports for the program is that a manifold's chart belongs to a coalition, which is what the record said of directions.

  - Phase coding survives its edges in every sequential model: against an end-to-end label-shuffle null (top-20 rows for days: GPT-2 small 0.36 against a 95th percentile of 0.13, Qwen2.5-0.5B 0.34, SmolLM2-135M 0.28, OLMo-1B 0.17, OPT-125m 0.58, nulls 0.10 to 0.16), falling smoothly with the number of rows taken and reaching the null by 500 rows (GPT-2 small 0.46, 0.36, 0.20, 0.13 for the top 5, 20, 100, 500), transferring across template halves within 0.06, and sharpening with scale (GPT-2 small, medium, large 0.36, 0.51, 0.70; OPT-125m to 1.3b 0.58 to 0.76), while the three Pythias sit at the null for days (-0.04, -0.03, -0.02) and within 0.03 of it for months (0.09, 0.08, 0.07 against nulls of 0.06, 0.06, 0.12).
  - Session 129's reading that the embedding's ring is abandoned is withdrawn: the embedding's pattern on its own plane is carried and amplified in place in most pairs (energy at block 2 relative to the embedding's own: Pythias 5.89 to 10.14, OLMo-1B 6.23, GPT-2 small 3.61, OPT-125m 1.02, at cosines 0.92 to 1.00; Qwen2.5-0.5B days 1.82 at 0.78, SmolLM2-135M days 2.93 at 0.64) while the whole state grows faster, so the share fell but the ring did not; it is reversed, not merely cancelled, for the months of both Qwens (cosine -0.16 at block 2 falling to -0.76 by block 8 at 7.96 times the energy, the block-0 MLP writing -0.78 of the pattern) and weakly for SmolLM2-360M months (0.17 at block 2, -0.24 at block 5).
  - Pre-registered: E1 (phase coding survives an end-to-end label-shuffle null: in the four models that showed it, the observed top-20 cosine is above the 95th percentile of 100 shuffles) confirmed; E2 (it is a population, not a handful: the alignment decreases smoothly with the number of rows taken (top 5 above top 20 above top 100 above top 500) and the top 500 is still above the shuffle null) refuted; E3 (it transfers across templates: rows selected on one half of the templates keep at least 70 percent of their in-sample alignment against the plane and angles fitted on the other half) confirmed; E4 (the family split holds: Pythia-1.4b (parallel residual) lacks phase coding (below 0.1) while OPT-125m, OPT-1.3b, GPT-2 medium and SmolLM2-360M (sequential) show it above 0.15) confirmed; E5 (the embedding's ring is outgrown rather than erased in Pythia-160m's weekdays (the absolute energy of the block-2 pattern projected on the embedding plane is at least 0.7 of the embedding pattern's own energy) and erased in Qwen2.5-0.5B's months (below 0.3)) refuted; E6 (the day-arithmetic task (Today is X. Tomorrow is) is solved at 0.7 or better among the seven day tokens by Qwen2.5-0.5B and OLMo-1B, and at 0.3 or worse by Pythia-160m and GPT-2 small) refuted; E7 (the population is causal: zeroing the write columns of the top-20 phase-coded rows per day (their union, at most 140 rows) halves the ring's radius at the best block and lowers day-arithmetic accuracy by 0.3 or more where the task is solved, while the same number of random rows changes neither by more than 0.05) refuted; E8 (OLMo-1B's four month rows are real: selected on one half of the templates they carry 0.4 or more of the month pattern on the other half, and their write directions put month tokens among the top 20 of the unembedding reading) refuted. E2 fails on its second clause: by 500 rows the alignment is at the null in GPT-2 small, Qwen and OLMo-1B, so the population is a few hundred rows, not thousands. E5 fails because its criterion assumed cancellation would show as low energy; the energy stays and the cosine flips. E6 fails on both sides: Qwen's days are at 0.57 and GPT-2 small solves the task at 0.79. E7 fails because the phase-coded rows are not the ring's carrier (their removal takes 0.1 to 0.3 of the fixed-plane radius against 0.1 to 0.2 for random rows). E8 fails on its second clause only: OLMo-1B's four month rows carry half of the pattern on held-out templates but do not promote month tokens.

F3 is scored on the other rows' pattern after removal against the whole pattern before (the script's total after removal still used the original columns); the remaining rows recover at most a quarter of what was removed. F5 fails at half (a fall of 0.07) and holds at 90 percent (0.48).

  - Pre-registered: H1 (in the three Pythias the day-selective rows phase-code against the embedding plane's angles (0.15 or more, above the shuffle null) although not against the best block's plane) refuted; H2 (in the GPT-2 family the phase coding against the best plane exceeds that against the embedding plane by 0.15 or more) confirmed; H3 (in the sequential models the per-block phase coding against the best plane rises with depth toward the best block; in the Pythias it stays flat near zero at every block) refuted; H4 (the selective rows sit mostly in the blocks just before the best block in the sequential models, and mostly in the first two blocks in the Pythias) refuted. The two-regimes guess was wrong in its specifics: H1 fails because the Pythias' detectors phase-code in neither plane; H3 and H4 fail because the coding is highest at block 0 and the selective rows are block-0 rows in every model; the regimes differ in what block 0 writes.

- e651 THE COVERAGE OF THE SINGLE-ROW EDIT DETECTORS (a defender-side evaluation: e623's norm z-score and activation-consistency cosine plus e648b's read-write cosine, run blind on a model with one block-4 write row edited; edits of 8 high-use and 8 low-use rows, each scored by its behavioural effect, the mean next-token KL at the neuron's own top-firing positions, and by every detector's blind flag):

  | model | read-write cosine median (share below -0.1) | negate high-use: KL / flagged by read-write / by consistency | reflect high-use: KL / read-write / consistency | double flagged by norm | reflect low-use: KL / flagged by any |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-160m | -0.43 (0.76) | 0.01 / 1.00 / 0.33 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.67 | 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.25 |
  | Pythia-410m | -0.28 (0.76) | 0.01 / 0.40 / 0.80 | 0.01 / 0.00 / 0.80 | 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 |
  | Qwen2.5-0.5B | +0.40 (0.05) | 0.01 / 0.12 / 0.12 | 0.01 / 0.12 / 0.12 | 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.12 |
  | SmolLM2-135M | +0.24 (0.07) | 0.17 / 0.00 / 1.00 | 0.13 / 0.00 / 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.12 |

  - Editing a single block-4 write row and screening the edited model blind with three detectors (the norm z-score, e648b's read-write cosine, and an activation-consistency cosine), across two GELU models (Pythia-160m and -410m, read-write cosine median -0.43 and -0.28, 0.76 and 0.76 of rows below -0.1) and two gated models (Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2-135M, +0.40 and +0.24, only 0.05 and 0.07 below -0.1): the norm catches a doubled row everywhere; the read-write cosine catches a naive negate only in the GELU models and only partly (flagged 1.00 and 0.40 of high-use rows), because the flip makes a one-sided outlier only where the bulk is negative; a reflection of the write about its read axis, which keeps the norm and the read-write cosine unchanged by construction, evades both of those, but the activation-consistency detector flags it whenever the row carries behaviour (high-use reflections flagged by consistency 0.67, 0.80, 0.12, 1.00).
  - Reading, as a defender: across this battery no edit both changed behaviour appreciably and evaded every detector. The read-write cosine added in e648b has a real blind spot, the norm-and-cosine-preserving reflection, and is a GELU-only statistic, but the activation-consistency check covers that blind spot for exactly the rows that carry behaviour; the only edits that slip all three detectors are reflections of low-use rows, whose next-token effect at their own firing positions is near zero (KL about 0.00). So the three detectors are complementary: the norm covers scaling, the read-write cosine covers sign flips in GELU models, and consistency covers direction changes that preserve the geometry; the open gap is a reflection that is both behaviourally potent and consistency-clean, which this single-row battery did not find.
  - Pre-registered: V1 (the read-write cosine flags a naive negate in at least half of both row kinds (a flip sends the cosine from about -0.2 to +0.2)) refuted; V2 (the norm z-score flags doubling in at least half of both kinds) confirmed; V3 (the reflection evades the read-write cosine (flagged in at most 0.2), since it preserves that cosine by construction) confirmed; V4 (the reflection evades every one of the four detectors (flagged-any at most 0.2) for both kinds) refuted; V5 (the reflection still changes behaviour, its KL at least half the naive negate's, for both kinds) refuted. V1 fails because the read-write cosine's flag is a top-threshold recall that a single flipped row clears only sometimes, and never in the gated models. V4 fails, as the smoke already showed, because the activation-consistency detector catches the reflection on behaviour-carrying rows. V5 fails only in Pythia-160m, where the high-use reflection's KL is 0.43 of the negate's.

- e652 THE COALITION DETECTOR ROBUSTNESS (a seed high-use block-4 row and its k-1 most co-firing rows, k 1 to 32, each reflected about its read axis; behavioural KL at the coalition's firing positions; per-row recall of the norm, read-write cosine, single-row consistency and a coalition-aware consistency detector, all recomputed on the edited model's own states):

  | model | KL at k = 1 / 8 / 32 | single-row consistency recall k = 1 / 8 / 32 | coalition-consistency k = 32 | norm / read-write recall (any k) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-160m | 0.004 / 0.028 / 0.033 | 0.17 / 0.19 / 0.14 | 0.17 | <= 0.02 / 0.00 |
  | Pythia-410m | 0.003 / 0.030 / 0.039 | 0.17 / 0.06 / 0.03 | 0.03 | <= 0.08 / 0.00 |
  | SmolLM2-135M | 0.018 / 0.022 / 0.032 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.01 | 0.01 | <= 0.33 / 0.08 |

  - Distributing the e651 reflection across k co-firing block-4 rows (k up to 32) on three models did not reach the regime that would test Gemini 4's masking conjecture: the seed rows drawn from the 64 most-used carry little individual payload, so a single reflected row is caught by the consistency detector in only 0.17, 0.17 and 0.00 of seeds at k=1 (against the 0.67 to 1.00 of e651's high-payload rows), and its next-token KL is 0.004 to 0.018; the distributed edit's KL stays modest and roughly flat in k (0.003 to 0.039 in Pythia-410m), single-row consistency recall stays low at every k rather than collapsing from a high baseline, and the coalition-aware detector tracks the single-row one to within 0.03, neither needed nor helpful here; the norm and read-write cosine stay blind to the reflection as in e651.
  - Reading: the experiment is a null on its own terms, not evidence either way about distributed evasion. Because the chosen co-firing rows are individually near-invisible to begin with (low payload, uncaught at k=1), the single-row catch that the masking is supposed to defeat was never established, so whether co-firing hides a large distributed payload from consistency remains open; a clean test needs seeds that are individually caught (high payload) with the net payload held constant as it is spread. What does hold: the norm and read-write cosine are blind to a reflection at every k, consistent with e651.
  - Pre-registered: W1 (at k=1 the reflection is caught by single-row consistency in at least half the seeds (e651 replication)) refuted; W2 (the distributed edit keeps behavioural effect: KL at the largest k is at least the k=1 KL) confirmed; W3 (single-row consistency recall collapses at the largest k (<=0.2)) confirmed; W4 (the coalition-aware detector still catches the distributed edit (recall >=0.5 at the largest k)) refuted; W5 (the norm stays blind to the reflection at every k (recall <=0.2)) refuted. W1 fails because the top-use seed rows carry too little individual payload, which is the registered failure mode; with it unmet the masking test W3 and W4 are moot, and the experiment is recorded as a null.


SESSION 141 (2026-10-14, the Dell; the decisive check behind e652's null, after Gemini 4 traced it to e87. Hypothesis O1 fixed at 2026-10-14T13:38:43.)

- e652c WRITE ORTHOGONALITY OF CO-FIRING ROWS (a high-use block-4 row and its fifteen most co-firing rows are near-orthogonal in their write columns, mean absolute cosine 0.064 in Pythia-160m and 0.069 in Pythia-410m (median 0.062, 0.064; 95% and 85% of seeds below 0.1), the e87 result measured at this block):

  - Reading: this resolves the coalition-evasion question e652 left open. Gemini 4's masking needs the co-firing rows to shift one another's consistency context along their own write directions, and a distributed payload needs their writes to sum coherently toward one target; both require alignment, but co-active writes are near-orthogonal, so the distributed reflection loses payload (the KL collapse seen in e652 and e652b) and provides no masking. The single-row detector triangle of e651 is therefore robust to distribution across co-firing rows, for a structural reason already in the atlas, not an accident of construction.
  - Pre-registered: O1 (the mean |write cosine| between a seed and its co-firing rows is below 0.1 in most seeds, so the coalition-masking mechanism cannot operate) confirmed.

  | model | accuracy | wrong (hedge, content) | mask alone | peel | peel + mask | rotated peel + mask | random peel + mask | recurring peel + mask | prompt mean + mask | right kept by peel + mask | native union / masked logits, wrong |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- e655 THE FINAL LEDGER FROM TOP-M LOGPROBS ALONE (Gemini's idea 3, against DESIGN_PROXY section 2; 256 wikitext-2 test positions per model; prior art for M above D+1: Finlayson et al. 2024, Carlini et al. 2024):

  | model | D | ledger Jaccard, minimum norm, M = 20 / 64 / 256 / 1024 / 2048 | ledger Jaccard, OMP in logit space, M = 20 / 64 / 256 / 1024 | other-position control, M = 256 | largest word recovered, minimum norm / logit OMP, M = 20 | state cosine, minimum norm, M = 20 / 256 | reference vs hidden-state ledger | reference words from the last four blocks |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-160m | 768 | 0.03 / 0.04 / 0.08 / 0.98 / 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.01 / 0.05 | 0.003 | 0.29 / 0.01 | 0.30 / 0.64 | 0.23 | 0.58 |
  | Pythia-410m | 1024 | 0.01 / 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.67 / 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.02 | 0.003 | 0.11 / 0.00 | 0.20 / 0.41 | 0.35 | 0.46 |
  | Qwen2.5-0.5B | 896 | 0.01 / 0.01 / 0.02 / 1.00 / 1.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.01 / 0.03 | 0.001 | 0.03 / 0.00 | 0.14 / 0.35 | 0.27 | 0.66 |

  - With open weights the logits are a linear measurement of the post-final-norm state, so above D+1 logprobs the minimum-norm reconstruction is exact (state cosine 1.000 and the sixteen-word ledger identical at M = 2048 in all three models; Finlayson et al. 2024), and one equation short of it (M = 1024 in Pythia-410m, D = 1024) the state is 0.998 cosine-close yet only 0.67 of the ledger's words survive (its largest word at 0.96 of positions); from the top 20 to 256 logprobs an API usually returns, the reconstruction keeps the state's rough direction (cosine 0.14 to 0.64) and the ledger's largest word at 0.03 to 0.29 of positions at M = 20 (0.07 to 0.57 at 256), but almost none of its sixteen words (Jaccard 0.01 to 0.08, other-position control at most 0.003); Gemini's OMP directly in logit space is worse at every M (Jaccard at most 0.05, largest word at most 0.36); the top M beat M random tokens on the largest word at M = 20 in every model (0.29 against 0.10, 0.11 against 0.02, 0.03 against 0.00), but random tokens match or beat them in 3 of 9 model-and-M cells (Pythia-410m at M = 256: 0.38 against 0.16); and the ledger as the unembedding reads it shares only 0.23 to 0.35 of its words with the usual hidden-state ledger, 0.46 to 0.66 of them from the last four blocks.
  - Reading: DESIGN_PROXY's 'API-only models: nothing' is too strong for open weights: given more than D+1 logprobs per position the final state and its ledger come out exactly, which is linear algebra and prior art, not WDD. Below D, which covers every API's usual top 20, the sparse WDD prior does not rescue the inverse problem: the restricted signatures are too coherent for OMP, and the sixteen-word support is fragile even to a 0.998-cosine error, so only the largest word is legible, and only some of the time.
  - Pre-registered: B1 (at M = 20, OMP in logit space recovers the reference ledger's largest word at 50 percent or more of positions) refuted; B2 (at M = 20, OMP in logit space beats its other-position control by 0.10 or more in support Jaccard) refuted; B3 (the sparse prior helps when underdetermined: OMP in logit space beats the minimum-norm reconstruction in Jaccard at both M = 64 and M = 256) refuted; B4 (above D+1 logprobs (M = 2048) the minimum-norm reconstruction recovers the state (cosine 0.99 or more) and the ledger (Jaccard 0.95 or more)) confirmed; B5 (the ledger as the unembedding reads it agrees with the usual hidden-state ledger (Jaccard 0.5 or more)) refuted; B6 (60 percent or more of the reference ledger's words come from the last four blocks) split (holds in Qwen2.5-0.5B, not Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m).

The second traversal of a friendly middle block re-runs the first's computation with the same words and signs, e509's amplification rather than LOOPED.md's erasure, which is why simply adding the band's increment again in one pass reproduces the repeat. WDD adds nothing beyond the plain baselines here: its support overlap predicts the map worse than the centred cosine in all three models (only the weights-only reader compatibility wins, and only in Pythia-410m), its chord is a worse virtual repeat than the raw increment, and its filtered junction is never the best fix.
  - Pre-registered: P1 (on the least damaging blocks the second traversal's band increment points along the first's (mean cosine above 0.3)) confirmed; P2 (half or more of the first traversal's eight largest MLP writes per token are gone from the second's eight largest) confirmed; P3 (the second-to-first MLP output cosine is lower in Pythia-410m (GELU, read repulsion) than in both gated models) refuted; P4 (the least damaging blocks show a higher second-to-first MLP output cosine than the most damaging ones) confirmed.

  - Clamping the chain rows' activations to one pole's sign at every position forces that pole in one direction only: it moves 0.67 of female items to male, 0.93 of plurals to singular and 0.26 of the younger generation to the older while keeping every item already at the target (kept 1.00, 1.00, 1.00), but moves 0.03, 0.05 and 0.00 the other way, although 5 of 5 gender rows and 5 of 6 number rows change sign by pole; where it works it costs far less off-target than a steering vector matched in effect (wikitext KL 0.001 against 4.69 for gender, 0.004 against 1.48 for number, 0.002 against 0.007 for generation; she-minus-he shift -0.11 against +0.67), although the rows are not silent on ordinary text (their mean absolute activation on wikitext is 0.07 to 0.23 of that at the words).
  - Reading: the clamp is the conditional edit Gemini proposed and it is far cleaner than a dense steering vector, but it is one-way: the rows can be turned to write the unmarked form (male, singular, older) and not the marked one (female, plural, younger), which fits rows that fire strongly for the marked form and weakly otherwise, so a sign clamp can invert an active signal but not create an absent one.
  - Pre-registered: K1 (the clamp moves at least 0.3 of the other pole's held-out gender items to the target while keeping at least 0.9 of the target pole's, forcing either pole) refuted; K2 (wherever the clamp moves at least 0.2 of the items, the steering vector at the matched scale costs more wikitext KL than the clamp) confirmed; K3 (for gender, wherever the clamp moves at least 0.2 of the items, the matched steering vector shifts the she-minus-he logit on neutral wikitext more than the clamp) confirmed; K4 (the chain rows' mean absolute activation on wikitext is under a tenth of that at the attribute words, for all three attributes (the self-gating premise)) refuted; K5 (suggested by the smoke: the clamp works one way only, moving at least 0.2 of the items for one pole and under 0.1 for the other, for every attribute) confirmed.

Where the rows are one-pole detectors, removing the mark is nearly free and one-way, and adding it costs about what a dense steering vector costs, because the signal has to be injected rather than inverted (e660's three orders of magnitude belong to stripping, not to setting). The WDD vote's real contribution is finding the blocks where an attribute is written: within them the top activation-difference row does as well, and ranked by activation difference alone the search lands in blocks that do not carry it.
