  - The pre-MLP residual (block input plus attention) is unchanged by every edit, the other rows' statistic moves by at most 1e-07, and negation and reflection negate the edited row's value exactly (to 9e-08), as Gemini derived; but the high-use rows' clean values sit in the tails (median clean percentile 0.80, 0.89, 0.01, 0.99 in Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, SmolLM2-135M) without clearing the opposite tail once flipped, so the check flags high-use reflections in 0.00, 0.40, 0.38, 0.50 of rows (two-sided at a 1% budget), pooled 0.29 over 21 rows, against 0.33 for e667's honest consistency and 0.43 for the two together; SmolLM2-135M row 776 (clean +0.19, percentile 0.98, flipped to -0.19 against a 0.5th percentile of -0.30) is not caught; one-sided, as Gemini framed it (the phase turning negative), the pooled rate is 0.19, because in Qwen2.5-0.5B the high-use rows sit in the lower tail and their flips show as positive outliers: among them Qwen2.5-0.5B row 3340 (KL 0.036), which no other check flags.
  - Reading: the construction is sound, with no feedback from the tamper and an exact sign flip, and it adds a row that no earlier check sees in Qwen2.5-0.5B, but it does not close the reflection hole: a sign flip shows only when the clean value is already beyond the opposite tail, which most high-use rows are not. Like the norm and the read-write cosine it is a scalar screen that a defender can add, not a guarantee against an attacker who knows it.
  - Pre-registered: P1 (Gemini's claim: pooled over the four models, C_perp (raw, two-sided) flags the high-use reflections in at least 0.6 of rows, against 0.33 for e667's honest consistency) refuted; P2 (Gemini's case: C_perp (raw, two-sided) flags SmolLM2-135M row 776's reflection, which evades all three detectors in e667) refuted; P3 (the analytic part: every edit leaves the pre-MLP residual unchanged (tolerance 1e-3) and the other rows' C_perp unchanged (1e-3), and negation and reflection negate the edited row's C_perp exactly (1e-3)) confirmed; P4 (why it can fail: the high-use rows' clean C_perp sits inside the bulk, median clean percentile between 0.2 and 0.8 on every model, so the exact sign flip lands inside the bulk as well) refuted.

- e668 PRE-WDD (Qwen2.5-0.5B; targets the top direct-contribution row of each attribute; upstream = every MLP write column of the blocks below the target; held-out translation flips from the marked pole; selectivity = |pole activation change| over its standard deviation, percentile among all upstream rows):

  | upstream rows negated (target untouched) | gender row: flips at 8 / 32 rows, target's held-out activation at 32 | number row: flips at 8 / 32 rows, target's activation at 32 | selectivity percentile of the top 32, gender / number |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | up read vector, |cos| (Gemini's one-line baseline) | 0.14 / 0.12, x0.58 | 0.12 / 0.95, x0.19 | 0.50 / 0.96 |
  | up read vector, raw dot product | 0.14 / 0.12, x0.58 | 0.25 / 0.47, x0.72 | 0.62 / 0.92 |
  | gate read vector, |cos| | 0.14 / 0.17, x0.52 | 0.95 / 0.95, x0.20 | 0.62 / 0.98 |
  | OMP on the up read vector | 0.09 / 0.10, x0.77 | 0.10 / 0.07, x0.87 | 0.40 / 0.63 |
  | data-driven, through the up | 0.19 / 0.29, x0.44 | 0.90 / 0.97, x0.17 | 0.86 / 1.00 |
  | data-driven, through the gate | 0.28 / 0.28, x0.39 | 0.95 / 0.97, x0.24 | 0.92 / 1.00 |
  | random rows of the same blocks (three draws) | 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 to 0.05 | 0.55 to 0.63 / 0.44 to 0.50 |
  | the target row itself | 0.52 | 0.38 | |

  - From the weights alone (each upstream write column's cosine with the target's read vector times the input norm gain, no data), negating the 32 best-aligned upstream rows with the target untouched flips 0.95 of held-out plurals through the number row (block 7, row 870), nearly as many as the data-driven feeders (0.97) and more than negating the target itself (0.38; random rows 0.00 to 0.05); with the gate's read vector 8 rows suffice (0.95); through the gender row (block 4, row 3019) the same flips 0.12 (gate 0.17) against 0.29 for the data-driven feeders and 0.52 for the target itself, and the nominees are no more attribute-selective than random rows (median selectivity percentile 0.50 against 0.55 to 0.63); across all upstream rows the alignment does not predict attribute selectivity (Spearman -0.004 to 0.023), so what works is the extreme top of the ranking, where for number the best-aligned rows are the rows that carry it (top-8 overlap with the data-driven gate feeders 0.78, gender 0.23); OMP on the same read vector does worse than the one-line ranking (number, 32 rows: 0.07 against 0.95); against the token embeddings the read vector separates the two poles' English answer words only through the gender row's gate (AUC 0.98; up 0.39; number 0.39 and 0.52), and its top tokens are noise.
  - Reading: Pre-WDD is one row of the virtual weights (Elhage et al. 2021) read with a norm-folded input, and its token side is the zero-pass projection of Dar et al. (2023); as a tracer it works where an attribute is relayed by MLP rows that write and read one direction (number in Qwen2.5-0.5B) and fails where it is not (gender at block 4), with no global relation between alignment and function to fall back on. Gemini's 'WDD squared' is the same virtual-weight matrix iterated (Voss et al. 2021's expanded weights), whose interference Ameisen et al. (2025) and Turner et al. (2026) document, and 'imaginary WDD' is the polar form of two real projections, notation unless its phase predicts something they do not; neither was run.
  - Pre-registered: H1 (Gemini's one-line baseline at k = 32: negating the top 32 upstream rows by |cos| with the target's up read vector, the target untouched, flips at least half as many held-out marked items as the data-driven top 32 through the up path, on both targets) split (holds for number, not gender); H2 (the gate read vector at k = 32: the top 32 by |cos| with the gate read vector flip at least half as many held-out marked items as the data-driven top 32 through the gate, on both targets) confirmed; H3 (above random at k = 32: each data-free nominee set (up cos, raw, gate cos, OMP) flips at least 0.1 more held-out marked items than the mean of three random draws of 32 upstream rows, on both targets) split (holds for gender, not number); H4 (OMP adds nothing at k = 32: OMP's flips are within 0.05 of the one-line up |cos| nominees' or below, on both targets) confirmed.

  - Reading: the pre-registered test supports Gemini's direction claim, weakly: frozen trained write directions raise the chance of grokking within 20000 steps over random directions, and not through their norms (random directions at the trained norms grok in one run of five); but the effect is about the size of the seed-to-seed spread, so e576's single permuted run was a draw from that spread rather than a takeoff distinct from its trained run, and every frozen arm groks far later than the unfrozen network.
  - Pre-registered: G1 (Gemini's claim: with the rows frozen at the trained directions (trained and permuted pooled, ten runs) the median step at which test accuracy first reaches 0.5 is at least 2000 steps earlier than with random directions at the trained norms (random_normmatched, five runs)) confirmed; G2 (Gemini's reading of the permuted run: at least 6 of the 10 trained-direction runs reach test accuracy 0.9 within 20000 steps) confirmed; G3 (the seed point: trained and permuted are one experiment: the difference between their median steps to test 0.5 is smaller than the larger of the two conditions' ranges across seeds) confirmed; G4 (norm alone: random directions at the trained norms reach test 0.5 at a median at least 2000 steps earlier than e576's initial-scale random rows) refuted.

  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

  | k-means routes, all sampled neurons | 300 | 0.61 | 0.50 (p 0.48) | 1.9e-03 / 1.9e-03 | 1.39 / 1.36 | 0.58 (p 0.0033) | 0.59 (p 0.0016) | 0.73 |
  | by the upstream neuron adding most (the essay's figure) | 273 | 0.19 | 0.45 (p 0.97) | 1.8e-03 / 2.0e-03 | 1.40 / 1.38 | 0.57 (p 0.011) | 0.54 (p 0.091) | 0.72 |

  - 3024 of block 6's 3072 neurons have a substantial top 100 (the 100th firing at least a quarter of the maximum); for 300 of them, sampled, the top firings split exactly through the LayerNorm (largest relative error 6e-04) show a median pre-activation of 1.48 built from upstream MLP neurons 0.53, attention 1.12 and the embedding 0.01 (plus constants); 83 of 300 neurons (0.28) have two routes that beat a unimodal null with the same mean and covariance (silhouette median 0.31 against the null's 0.30, its 95th percentile 0.36), the core holding a median 0.67 of the top 100; by the essay's grouping the most common top upstream neuron carries a median 0.19; removing the neuron moves the next-token distribution less at offshoot firings than at core firings in 0.45 of multi-route neurons (p 0.86; median KL 2.0e-03 core, 2.3e-03 offshoot) and in 0.45 by the essay's grouping (p 0.97); over training the final top-100 firings climb from a median percentile of 0.608 at step 128 to 0.999 at the end (128 0.608, 256 0.639, 512 0.718, 1000 0.788, 2000 0.880, 4000 0.939, 8000 0.970, 16000 0.987, 32000 0.994, 64000 0.998, 143000 0.999); the core's firings were top firings earlier than the offshoot's, final activation regressed out, in 0.53 of multi-route neurons (p 0.33) and in 0.57 by the essay's grouping (p 0.011; 0.54 with the token's typicality also regressed out).

  - Reading: at Pythia-160m's block 6 neither of the essay's reasons not to worry about recursive generalization holds for distinct routes: offshoot firings matter as much per firing as core firings (by the essay's own grouping slightly more), and two-route neurons form neither route first; the order the essay describes shows up instead inside a single route, its bulk becoming top firings before the rest of its top firings, a pattern found after the fact and not pre-registered; the essay's grouping's early lead is mostly token identity, its main upstream neuron often a token detector whose contexts are learned early as tokens are; the cleanest two-route neurons are unrelated token pairs, the small-model polysemanticity the essay sets apart from recursive generalization.
  - Pre-registered: P1 (developmental, cluster split, multi-route neurons: the core's firings became top firings earlier than the offshoot's, final activation regressed out: lead positive in more than half, one-sided binomial p < 0.05 (REFUTED if the share is below half with p < 0.05 the other way; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED)) refuted; P2 (causal, cluster split, multi-route neurons: removing the neuron moves the next-token distribution less at offshoot firings than at core firings (mean KL) in more than half, one-sided binomial p < 0.05; 'much less' when the median offshoot/core KL ratio is below 0.5) refuted; R1 (replication of the smoke: top-upstream split, testable neurons, the residualized lead positive in more than half with p < 0.05, and still p < 0.05 with token typicality also regressed out) refuted; D1 (descriptive: the share of sampled neurons that are multi-route under the cluster split lies between 0.05 and 0.25 (the essay's reference: about 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron poles have one main job)) refuted.

  - Pre-registered: L1a (the essay, every double-negative activation: zeroing them in every layer gives more repairs than damages on more than half of the eight non-generative benchmarks, in each model) refuted; L1b (the essay, the leak-dominated neurons only: the same for leak0_dom, in each model) refuted; L2 (the reasoning part: zeroing the double negative in every layer lowers GSM8K accuracy (more damages than repairs, exact binomial p < 0.05) in each model whose base GSM8K accuracy is at least 0.10) confirmed; L3 (specificity: zeroing the double negative raises wikitext loss less than the L2-matched weak gate-open control, in each model) refuted; L4 (depth: zeroing it in the second half of the layers raises wikitext loss less than in the first half, in each model) confirmed; M1 (replacing the double negative with its per-neuron mean raises wikitext loss less than half as much as zeroing it, in each model) confirmed; M2 (the essay's claim under the gentlest ablation: mean replacement of the double negative everywhere gives more repairs than damages on more than half of the eight non-generative benchmarks, in each model) refuted.

  | Pythia-160m block (Pythia-410m blocks searched) | two-route of 300 | two-route neurons whose routes find different 410m specialists | random splits of the same firings | one-route neurons that split | best single 410m neuron's coverage of the top 100, two-route / one-route (medians) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 3 (4-8) | 59 | 20 (0.34) | 0.00 | 46 of 241 (0.19) | 0.29 / 0.22 |
  | 6 (10-14) | 81 | 23 (0.28) | 0.00 | 37 of 219 (0.17) | 0.30 / 0.25 |
  | 9 (16-20) | 101 | 49 (0.49) | 0.00 | 47 of 199 (0.24) | 0.34 / 0.28 |

  - The two routes of a two-route Pythia-160m neuron find different Pythia-410m specialists, each covering its own route by at least 0.25 more than the other, in 0.34, 0.28, 0.49 of two-route neurons (blocks 3, 6, 9; pooled 92 of 241, against 0.7 expected from random splits of the same firings, p below 0.0001) and the bulk and rest of a one-route neuron in 0.19, 0.17, 0.24 (Fisher p below 0.0001); no single 410m neuron covers a 160m neuron's top firings closely: the best covers a median 0.29, 0.30, 0.34 of a two-route neuron's top 100 within its own top 1%, and 0.22, 0.25, 0.28 of a one-route neuron's.
  - Reading: the larger model does divide what a smaller model's two-route neurons do more often than it divides one-route neurons, as the essay's coarse-to-fine figures show for vision; but the correspondence is loose, no 410m neuron holding more than about a third of a 160m neuron's top firings, and the cleanest two-route neurons are unrelated token pairs (e672), so the split fits a capacity account as well as a branching one.
  - Pre-registered: K1 (pooled over the three blocks, two-route neurons split more often than random splits of the same firings predict (simulated Poisson-binomial tail p < 0.05)) confirmed; K2 (two-route neurons split more often than one-route neurons (one-sided Fisher exact p < 0.05)) confirmed; K3 (the best single Pythia-410m neuron covers a one-route neuron's top 100 better than a two-route neuron's (one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.05)) refuted.

  - A vector added after the middle block along a native write direction costs the next-token distribution no more than a random direction of the same norm, below the floor and above it: the position's own largest write scaled up by half a floor costs 0.97 to 1.58 of a random direction's KL across 5 models, by two floors 0.82 to 1.36; a foreign native row 0.99 to 1.02 at two floors; the rotated row at most 0.99 to 1.04 at any amplitude; the random direction's own cost grows with the square of the amplitude (median 0.00 to 0.00 nats at a quarter floor, 0.01 to 0.32 at four).
  - Reading: the floor is an identification bound, not a reader boundary, and native directions are not privileged: a foreign native row and its rotation cost what a random direction of the same norm costs at every amplitude from a quarter of a floor to four floors in every model, with no change of regime at one floor; only the position's own largest write differs, by model rather than by the floor (1.3 to 1.7 times a random direction below the floor in GPT-2 small, Pythia-410m, SmolLM2-135M and Qwen2.5-0.5B, 0.7 at four floors in Pythia-160m); the next block contracts every injected direction alike (area 05); so 'below the floor' says what a projection can identify, not what the readers ignore, and a reader's sensitivity to a direction is about the position's content, not its provenance.
  - Pre-registered: C1 (at 0.5 floors, own and foreign native injections cost the same next-token KL as a random direction (ratio in [0.7, 1.5])) split (holds for Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, SmolLM2-135M, not GPT-2 small); C2 (at 2 floors, the position's own write scaled up costs more than 2x a random direction) refuted; C3 (at 2 floors, a foreign native row costs the same as a random direction (e510/e511: a fake chord is contracted like noise)) confirmed; C4 (the rotated row equals random at every amplitude) confirmed.

  - Keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations by count (the essay's vision measure) and zeroing the rest costs 0.24 to 8.68 nats of next-token KL across 11 models while removing 0.03 to 0.37 of the activation energy; the strongest hundredth 0.34 to 14.52; by the essay's other measure, zeroing activations below a tenth of each neuron's maximum, 0.48 to 14.09 (below a fiftieth 0.01 to 0.16); replacing the removed activations by their per-neuron mean instead of zero costs 0.07 to 2.31; the dial tertile (the third of neurons with the least energy in their top 1% of positions) costs 0.10 to 1.85 against the detector tertile's 0.05 to 2.71; the predictions that flip have clean margins 0.07 against 0.31 for the rest (medians over models).
  - Reading: the essay's 'almost all weak activations can be removed for almost no cost' fails under zeroing: keeping the strongest quarter costs 0.2 to 8.7 nats, more at depth and in the larger models; in the GELU and GPT-2 models most of that cost is the removed activations' mean, which per-neuron mean replacement recovers (57 to 94 percent; 0.07 to 0.7 nats remain), in the gated models a minority of it (22 to 66 percent, none in SmolLM2-135M), whose signed SwiGLU activations have a less useful mean; what remains is token-specific, sitting in the dial tertile and the second half of the blocks of the gated models (ten to twenty times the detector tertile) and in the detector tertile of GPT-2 and Pythia, and the flips it causes are mostly near-ties; so weak activations matter as a bias the network depends on more than as a signal, e678's double negative generalised, and 'ablatable' is true only of their variation around that mean.
  - Pre-registered: W1 (keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations by count (the essay's vision measure) costs under 0.05 nats of KL) refuted; W1b (the same costs over 0.2 nats (Gao)) confirmed; W2 (the dial tertile (lowest top-1% energy share) costs at least twice the detector tertile) split (holds for OLMo-1B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, not GPT-2 small, GPT-2 large, GPT-2 medium, Pythia-160m, Pythia-1B, Pythia-410m); W3 (flipped predictions were near-ties: their clean margin's median is under half the unflipped median) split (holds for GPT-2 large, OLMo-1B, Pythia-160m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, not GPT-2 small, GPT-2 medium, Pythia-1B, Pythia-410m); W4 (the last block costs at least twice the average block per neuron) split (holds for Pythia-160m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, not GPT-2 small, GPT-2 large, GPT-2 medium, OLMo-1B, Pythia-1B, Pythia-410m); W5 (mean replacement is cheaper than zeroing) split (holds for GPT-2 small, GPT-2 large, GPT-2 medium, OLMo-1B, Pythia-160m, Pythia-1B, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-360M, not SmolLM2-135M).

  - A neuron's pre-activation at its strongest firings is the sum of 1874 to 15033 effective upstream contributors (weak firings 1861 to 16467), its sixteen largest inputs carrying 0.02 to 0.05 of it; the upstream writes that clear the floor at the position number 11.00 to 87.00 and carry 0.02 to 0.19 of the MLP input energy; driving the neuron by its sixteen largest inputs costs 0.43 to 2.11 of the damage of ablating it at its strong positions, by its 1024 largest 0.13 to 1.55, and the fewest inputs that halve the damage are never, 64, 16, never, never, 64, never, never, 256, 1024, 64, 64 across 12 model-block runs (every input reproduces the neuron: 0.00 to 0.01).
  - Reading: a mid-network neuron's input is a crowd of thousands, its sixteen largest inputs carry 2 to 5 percent of it, and the writes that clear the floor at the position carry 2 to 19 percent of the input energy, so the readers read mostly below the floor; driving the neuron by its sixteen largest inputs costs half to twice the damage of removing it (0.43 to 2.11 of it), and at blocks 12 and 18 of Pythia-410m and Qwen2.5-0.5B and block 12 of GPT-2 medium even its 1024 largest cannot halve that damage, because what they leave out is not a constant the mean could stand in for but position-specific (e685b); the pruned neuron attribution graph the essay expects to carry 'almost no error' carries, without an error term for the crowd, half to twice the error of deleting the node, which is the attribution-graph literature's error node made concrete at the neuron level, and Nanda's expectation; e685b adds the crowd's mean back as that error term and finds it a minority of the crowd's effect.
  - Pre-registered: L1 (the K=16 simulation's KL ratio is lower at the neuron's strong positions than over all positions) confirmed; L2_nick (at K=16 the median KL ratio at strong positions is under 0.25) refuted; L2_nanda (it is over 0.5) split (holds for GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 18, Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Pythia-410m block 6, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6, SmolLM2-135M block 15, SmolLM2-135M block 22, SmolLM2-135M block 8, not GPT-2 medium block 6); L3 (over-floor upstream writes carry more than half of the MLP input energy at strong firings) refuted.

  - With the crowd it leaves out replaced by its corpus mean, the sixteen-input simulation's KL at the strong positions falls from 0.48 to 2.09 to 0.41 to 1.53 of the ablation's across 4 model-blocks, the 64-input one from 0.41 to 2.66 to 0.31 to 2.41 and the 256-input one from 0.37 to 2.59 to 0.20 to 3.10; over all positions the sixteen-input simulation goes from 1.01 to 7.26 to 1.01 to 5.48.
  - Reading: the crowd below a neuron's largest inputs is not an offset: carrying its corpus mean as the attribution-graph error node removes a seventh to a quarter of the sixteen-input simulation's error at the strong firings (the ratio to the ablation's damage goes from 0.48 to 0.41 and 1.05 to 0.87 in Pythia-410m at blocks 6 and 12, 0.85 to 0.62 in GPT-2 medium at block 12 and 2.09 to 1.53 in Qwen2.5-0.5B at block 12) and never halves it; with the mean carried, 256 inputs still leave 0.20 to 3.10 of the ablation's damage, and in Qwen the mean makes the 256-input simulation worse (2.59 to 3.10) because the crowd's sum at a strong firing is anti-correlated with its largest terms there; so what the readers read in the crowd is its position-specific variation, and a neuron attribution graph pruned to its largest edges carries, even with the error node the literature gives it, two fifths to one and a half times the damage of deleting the node.
  - Pre-registered: L0 (every input reproduces the neuron (KL ratio under 0.05)) confirmed; L4 (adding the crowd's mean halves the K=16 KL ratio at strong positions) refuted; L5 (with the crowd's mean the K=16 ratio at strong positions is under 0.25) refuted; L6 (with the crowd's mean the K=64 ratio is under 0.25) refuted.

- e682 Are a learned fact's writers related to the fact (the essay) or an arbitrary store (Nanda): 200 facts and 50 random codes taught by the e643 recipe, the writers by direct contribution, their natural fields, their sharing and their depth:

  | model | steps, held-out accuracy (professions, cities), codes recalled | neutral loss change | writers firing on the fact's field (z above 3): facts / random neurons / delta-writers | codes / random | writer Jaccard: same value / same relation / different relation / codes among themselves | writers' depth, facts / codes | share of writers already top-16 in the base model | largest write-column cosine change |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-410m | 400, 1.00, 0.83, 0.68 | +0.034 | 0.42 / 0.14 / 0.50 | 0.25 / 0.11 | 0.337 / 0.045 / 0.004 / 0.127 | 0.83 / 0.78 | 0.45 | 0.0000 |
  | Qwen2.5-0.5B | 400, 0.99, 0.86, 0.76 | +0.008 | 0.56 / 0.16 / 0.57 | 0.59 / 0.22 | 0.379 / 0.055 / 0.038 / 0.231 | 0.96 / 0.98 | 0.42 | 0.0001 |

  - After 400 and 400 steps the models answer the held-out queries at 0.83 to 1.00 (codes recalled 0.68 to 0.76) at a neutral-text loss change of 0.01 to 0.03 nats; 0.42 to 0.56 of a fact's sixteen writers fire on natural Pile text about its value or relation (z above 3), against 0.14 to 0.16 for random neurons; writers of facts sharing a value overlap by Jaccard 0.34 to 0.38, of the same relation 0.04 to 0.06, of different relations 0.00 to 0.04; the random codes' writers fire on code-like text 0.25 to 0.59 of the time (random 0.11 to 0.22) and overlap among themselves by 0.13 to 0.23; the writers sit at a median depth of 0.83 to 0.96 of the network (codes 0.78 to 0.98), 0.42 to 0.45 of them were already the base model's top-16 at the same query, and no write column moved by more than 0.00 to 0.00 in cosine.
  - Reading: a learned fact's writers are neither an arbitrary store nor the fact's own circuit: facts that share a value share a third of their sixteen writers (Jaccard 0.34 in Pythia-410m, 0.38 in Qwen2.5-0.5B) and facts of different relations almost none (0.00, 0.04), the structure of a map of values and relations rather than a key-value database; 42 and 56 percent of a fact's writers fire on natural text about its value or relation against 14 and 16 percent for random neurons, three to four times chance and a majority only in Qwen; the random codes ride a shared code route (their writers overlap among themselves, 0.13 and 0.23, more than facts of one relation do) and fire on code-like text twice to three times as often as chance; everything sits in the last quarter of the network, no write column moves by more than a thousandth in cosine, and nearly half the writers were already the base model's strongest at the same query, Cammarata's off-ramp on existing routes rather than a new neuron, with routes that are related to the fact more often than chance and, in Pythia, unrelated more often than not.
  - Pre-registered: F1 (at least half of a fact's sixteen writers fire on natural Pile text about its value or relation (z > 3)) split (holds for Qwen2.5-0.5B, not Pythia-410m); F1b (random neurons do so under 0.1) refuted; F2 (facts sharing a value share writers more than twice as much (Jaccard) as facts of different relations) confirmed; F3 (the random codes' writers are related to a code-like field at most half as often as facts' writers to theirs) refuted; F3b (the codes share writers among themselves at least as much as facts of one relation do (packing)) confirmed; F4 (the writers' median depth is in the last third) confirmed; F5 (no write column changes by more than 0.02 in cosine (existing routes, no rewritten row)) confirmed.

- e683 Chain, star or jump: does a neuron's class grow by offshoots of offshoots (recursive generalization), from the core, or by unrelated jumps, over Pythia-160m's checkpoints in three seeds?:

  | run | neurons, entrants | nearest prior member in attribution space: chain / old / jump | expected chain, enrichment, share of neurons above 1.5 | in state space: chain / jump, enrichment | one-token share of the root (step 1000) against the final top-20 | two-route neurons: offshoot members entered by chain more than core's |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-160m | 200, 150413 | 0.49 / 0.50 / 0.01 | 0.53, 0.92, 0.00 | 0.51 / 0.01, 0.96 | 0.20 vs 0.15 (0.55 of neurons) | 42: 0.60 |
  | Pythia-160m seed 1 | 200, 150044 | 0.48 / 0.50 / 0.02 | 0.53, 0.91, 0.00 | 0.51 / 0.01, 0.96 | 0.20 vs 0.20 (0.49 of neurons) | 37: 0.62 |
  | Pythia-160m seed 2 | 200, 150875 | 0.49 / 0.49 / 0.01 | 0.53, 0.92, 0.00 | 0.52 / 0.01, 0.98 | 0.20 vs 0.15 (0.54 of neurons) | 34: 0.59 |

  - Over 451332 entries into 600 neurons' top-1% classes across 3 seeds, the entrant's nearest prior member by input attribution had itself entered within the last two checkpoints in 0.48 to 0.49 of cases against 0.53 to 0.53 expected from the members' ages (enrichment 0.91 to 0.92, above 1.5 for 0.00 to 0.00 of neurons); the nearest member was below the random-position null (a jump) in 0.01 to 0.02; in block-6 state space the same chain share is 0.51 to 0.52 and the jump share 0.01 to 0.01; the root class at step 1000 has a one-token share of 0.20 to 0.20 against 0.15 to 0.20 at 16000; among two-route neurons the minor route's members entered by chain more often than the core's in 0.59 to 0.62.
  - Reading: growth is adjacent but not a chain: a new context's nearest existing member by input attribution is a recent entrant exactly as often as the members' ages predict (enrichment 0.91 to 0.92 in three seeds, above 1.5 for no neuron) and is below the random-position null in 1 to 2 percent of entries, in attribution space and in state space alike; the essay's branch of branches ('iy' to 'diy' to 'do it yourself') does not appear as an order of arrivals in Pythia-160m's top-1% classes, while its 'nothing unrelated' does; the root at step 1000 is at most a little more token-concentrated than the final class, and the minor route of a two-route neuron entered by chain no more than the core; one caveat bounds the test: half of a top-1% class turns over each checkpoint, so most entries are margin churn, and a magnitude-defined core would be the sharper test.
  - Pre-registered: G1 (chain enrichment (new contexts nearest a member that entered within two checkpoints, over the random expectation) exceeds 1.5 in at least 70% of neurons) refuted; G2 (the median jump share (nearest member below the random-position null) is under 0.15) confirmed; G3 (the root (top-20 at step 1000) is more one-token concentrated than the final top-20) split (holds for Pythia-160m, Pythia-160m seed 2, not Pythia-160m seed 1); G4 (in two-route neurons the minor route's members entered by chain more often than the core's, in at least 60%) split (holds for Pythia-160m seed 1, not Pythia-160m, Pythia-160m seed 2).

- e684 Do readers arrive after a row is recruited (the essay's buildability): downstream readers of a recruited word's write before and after recruitment, against norm-matched and random rows, their alignment with the row against the class direction, and sub-class specialists:

  | run | recruited words | readers (share above 0.2 std) two checkpoints before -> after | the word's reader gain beats its norm-matched control rows: count / top-10 mean share / mass | readers' alignment gain with the row vs the class direction (row above class) | sub-class specialists before -> after (random-set null after; gain above null) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Pythia-160m | 139 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 0.33 / 0.79 / 0.81 | 0.026 vs 0.005 (0.97) | 119.0 -> 119.5 (0.0; 0.46) |
  | Pythia-160m seed 1 | 150 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 0.26 / 0.76 / 0.77 | 0.032 vs 0.007 (0.94) | 127.0 -> 127.5 (0.0; 0.49) |
  | Pythia-160m seed 2 | 151 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 0.26 / 0.75 / 0.75 | 0.027 vs 0.005 (0.91) | 104.0 -> 118.0 (0.0; 0.41) |

  - For 440 words recruited between checkpoints 3000 and 14000 in three seeds, the count of later-block neurons reading the row at a fifth of their pre-activation spread goes from a median 0.00 to 0.00 two checkpoints before recruitment to 0.00 to 0.00 two after; the word's gain beats its norm-matched control rows on the same positions in 0.26 to 0.33 of words by count, 0.75 to 0.79 by the ten strongest readers' mean share and 0.75 to 0.81 by total reader mass; the readers' alignment with the row rises by 0.03 to 0.03 against 0.00 to 0.01 with the class direction (the row ahead in 0.91 to 0.97); sub-class specialists go from 104.00 to 127.00 to 118.00 to 127.50 (random position sets 0.00 to 0.00), the gain beating the null's in 0.41 to 0.49.
  - Reading: readers follow recruitment, weakly: the ten strongest downstream readers of a recruited row gain share across the recruitment relative to norm-matched rows on the same positions in three quarters to four fifths of words, the total reader mass likewise, and the readers' alignment moves toward the row rather than the class direction in nine tenths or more; but no reader ever depends on the row at a fifth of its own spread (the counts stay at zero before and after), and sub-class specialists do not multiply beyond chance; so the essay's buildability is visible as a slow redistribution of many readers' weights toward the recruited parameter, not as the arrival of a dedicated reader, which is what e591's 'recruitment is not a performance event' looks like from the readers' side.
  - Pre-registered: R1 (the recruited row gains readers (|share| > 1 std) from two checkpoints before to two after, more than norm-matched control rows on the same positions, in at least 65% of words) refuted; R1b (the ten strongest readers' mean share gains more across recruitment than the norm-matched control rows' on the same positions, in at least 65% of words) confirmed; R1c (the total reader mass gains more than the control rows' in at least 65% of words) confirmed; R2 (the readers' alignment gain with the row exceeds their gain with the class direction in at least 60%) confirmed; R3 (sub-class specialists among later-block neurons increase across recruitment more than for random position sets in at least 60%) refuted.

  - At the middle block a surface rule (current token, previous token, bigram tables fitted to the neuron's own class) covers 0.00 to 0.01 of a neuron's held-out class at precision 0.5 and 0.00 to 0.00 at precision 0.8 (medians over neurons, 4 models); precision at recall 0.9 is 0.01 to 0.01, at recall 0.5 0.01 to 0.02; 0.09 to 0.14 of held-out class positions carry a token and a bigram that never fired in training; a rule reaching recall 0.9 at precision 0.5 on the training text exists for 0.77 to 0.97 of neurons with a median size of 359.00 to 383.50 entries, and the most common token covers 0.07 to 0.08 of a class.

  - Pinning gender and number onto one quiet row of Pythia-160m block 4 at step 8000 installs both at the pin's end in 4 of 5 seeds (vote shares 0.78 to 1.00 gender, 0.92 to 1.00 number; dials -0.00 to 0.12 and -0.00 to 0.34); after 6000 steps of the next-token loss alone the vote shares are 0.72 to 1.00 and 0.89 to 1.00, a concept shed (below 0.5) in 0 of 5 and both kept (0.8 or more) in 4; the dials end at -0.00 to 0.06 and -0.00 to 0.06; the single-concept pins keep their vote share through the release in 4 of 4.
  - Reading: as a description, arbitrary packing is stable: a quiet row pinned to carry both gender and number at step 8000 takes both votes in four of five seeds and keeps both through 6000 steps of the next-token loss alone in every seed, exactly as the single-concept pins keep theirs, so the essay's semantic gravity does not unpack a knot that gradient descent did not make; as a mechanism, the pin mostly installs a description: where it created a dial (three of five knots, two of four singles) the dial decays through the release by the same factor in knots and singles, and in the rest no dial ever existed, e627's lesson again; so the knot test refutes instability and cannot separate packed from single on behaviour.
  - Pre-registered: K1 (both concepts install at the pin's end (vote share at least 0.8 each) in at least 4 of 5 seeds) confirmed; K2_gravity (by release step 6000 at least one vote share falls below 0.5 in at least 3 of 5 seeds) refuted; K2_stable (both stay at least 0.8 in at least 3 of 5 seeds) confirmed; K3 (single-concept pins keep vote share at least 0.8 through release in at least 3 of 4 runs) confirmed; K4 (a shed concept's dial is under 0.03 (dials follow votes)) not testable (no concept shed).

  - Reading: the crowd can be summarised without training where it is shallow or lexical, and nowhere else: at the sixth block of Pythia-410m, GPT-2 medium and Qwen2.5-0.5B a per-token table of the crowd (held-out text) brings the sixteen-input simulation to 0.16 to 0.46 of the ablation damage and the crowd of the nearest same-token position in those sixteen inputs to 0.24 to 0.44, each for most neurons; at GPT-2 medium's block 12 the table still halves it (0.35); at Pythia-410m's blocks 12 and 18 only the neighbour does, for half the neurons (medians 0.47 to 0.50 against 0.60 to 0.92 for the table and 0.78 to 1.22 for a random same-token position), so there the crowd is partly a function of the sparse part, missing magnitude rather than missing information; at Qwen2.5-0.5B's block 12 and SmolLM2-135M's block 15 nothing training-free halves it (best 0.77 to 1.20); the sixteen largest guilds summed exactly do as well as random groups of the same sizes (write-row guilds beat random in one block of eight) and at group resolution, one edge per guild, they do nothing, so there is no guild structure in the weights or in co-activation that a reader's input exploits; the stream's principal directions do nothing; the crowd's 200 largest contributors have classes containing the neuron's strong rows at 1.3 to 2.5 times chance, not a district; and at the strong firings the crowd's net sum is mostly each upstream unit's corpus mean (0.27 to 0.92), token-specific only at the shallow blocks (0.32 to 0.50) and contextual up to 0.42 at depth.

  - The sixteen-input simulation swapped in only off the neuron's top-5% positions carries 0.52 to 0.88 of its all-position damage across 8 model-blocks, and only at those positions 0.10 to 0.61 (ratios over all positions 0.40 to 6.10 against 0.18 to 0.88); sixteen excitatory wires alone cost 0.68 to 90.54 of the ablation damage at the strong firings and 5.88 to 561.34 over all positions, sixteen excitatory with sixteen inhibitory 0.59 to 1.06 (thirty-two by magnitude 0.38 to 2.30, sixteen 0.41 to 1.95); the crowd's write on the upstream weak-write bus (96 to 288 directions) brings the sixteen wires to 0.29 to 0.93 at the strong firings and 0.58 to 2.58 over all positions (from 0.83 to 7.00), the signed wires with the bus to 0.37 to 0.73; the crowd's net sum over the sixteen wires is -0.72 to -0.10 of theirs off the class and -0.30 to 0.38 on it, and the sixteen inhibitory wires carry 0.87 to 1.35 of the off-class opposition.
  - Reading: the brake is causal and it is position-specific: swapping the sixteen-input simulation in only off a neuron's top-5% positions carries 0.78 to 0.88 of its all-position damage at the mid-depth blocks (0.52 to 0.64 at the sixth blocks), while at those positions alone it carries 0.10 to 0.20; sixteen excitatory wires by themselves fire the neuron everywhere, costing 6 to 561 times the ablation damage over all positions; adding the sixteen strongest inhibitory wires, which carry 0.87 to 1.35 of the net opposition at each position, halves the all-position damage at mid-depth (3.0 from 5.6 and 7.0 in Pythia-410m and Qwen2.5-0.5B at block 12) but leaves the firings at 0.59 to 1.06 of the ablation damage, because a few wires cannot cancel a large excitation to the small net the model has; the crowd's write on the upstream blocks' weak-write subspaces (sixteen directions per block, e693's bus, 96 to 288 directions) halves both the firing and the all-position ratios at the four mid-depth blocks where the stream's own directions did nothing in e692 (0.35 to 0.93 at the firings from 0.74 to 1.95, 1.1 to 2.6 over all positions from 4.2 to 7.0), and signed wires with the bus is the best training-free graph everywhere (0.37 to 0.73 at the firings, 0.62 to 1.75 over all positions) without reaching the essay's almost no error anywhere; so the error node a pruned neuron graph needs is the brake, the brake lives in the weak-write subspace of the upstream blocks, and sixteen wires of either sign cannot carry it.
  - Pre-registered: B0 (every input reproduces the neuron (ratio under 0.05)) confirmed; B1 (the simulation swapped in only off the neuron's top-5% positions carries at least 0.7 of the all-position damage) split (holds for Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6, SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 6); B1b (swapped in only at the top-5% positions it carries at most 0.3) split (holds for Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6, SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 6); B2 (the sixteen strongest excitatory with the sixteen strongest inhibitory inputs halve the sixteen-by-magnitude ratio at strong firings) split (holds for SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Pythia-410m block 6, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6); B2b (and beat thirty-two by magnitude by 0.1) split (holds for Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 6, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6); B3 (the sixteen wires plus the crowd's write on the upstream weak-write bus halve the ratio) split (holds for Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 6, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6); B4 (signed wires plus the bus bring the ratio under 0.25) refuted; B5 (the sixteen inhibitory wires carry at least half of the off-class net opposition) confirmed; B6 (the bus halves the all-position ratio) split (holds for Pythia-410m block 12, Pythia-410m block 18, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, SmolLM2-135M block 15, not GPT-2 medium block 12, GPT-2 medium block 6, Pythia-410m block 6, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 6).

  - At block 6 of Pythia-160m, for 100 of the final model's neurons followed by index, the crowd's net sum over the sixteen wires in the bottom half of positions goes from 0.28 to 0.30 of theirs at step 1000 to -0.76 to -0.60 in the final model across 3 seeds (Spearman with the step -1.00 to -0.99), the first checkpoint under -0.5 being 16000 for Pythia-160m block 6, 16000 for pythia160s1 b6, 16000 for pythia160s2 b6; at the core it goes from 0.69 to 0.93 to 0.14 to 0.22, the sixteen wires' net share at the core from 0.48 to 0.56 to 0.75 to 0.86, and the 1-5 percent shell's adjacent share from 0.56 to 0.59 to 0.55 to 0.58.
  - Reading: the brake is learned, early and gradually, and the drive sparsifies with it: at step 1000 of Pythia-160m the crowd's net sum off a neuron's class reinforces its sixteen wires (+0.28 to +0.30 of theirs), the sign flips by step 2000 (-0.15 to -0.19), the brake reaches -0.43 to -0.48 by step 8000, -0.50 to -0.53 by 16000 and -0.60 to -0.76 at the end of training, monotonically in three seeds (Spearman -0.99 to -1.00), while at the core the crowd goes from reinforcing (+0.69 to +0.93) to near neutral (+0.14 to +0.22) and the sixteen wires' net share of the drive rises from 0.48 to 0.56 to 0.75 to 0.86; the 1 to 5 percent shell's adjacency to the core dips from 0.57 at step 1000 to 0.46 at 2000 and recovers to 0.55 to 0.58; so training builds the sparse drive and the collective brake together, the same process e676 saw as growth from the centre, and the final model's crowd is the residue of that process rather than noise.
  - Pre-registered: T1 (at step 1000 the crowd's net sum off the class is within 0.3 of the sixteen wires' (no brake)) split (holds for pythia160s1 b6, pythia160s2 b6, not Pythia-160m block 6); T2 (the brake (under -0.5) is present by step 8000) refuted; T3 (the brake strengthens monotonically with the step (Spearman under -0.8)) confirmed; T4 (the sixteen wires' net share at the core rises with training (Spearman above 0.5)) confirmed; T5 (the brake is under -0.5 in the final model) confirmed.

  - With all but the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations zeroed at every block at once, the true weak write on its sixteen principal directions recovers 0.66 to 0.96 of the zeroing cost across 8 models, and a rank-16 bypass that predicts those coordinates linearly from the normalised block input, without running the weak neurons, recovers 0.56 to 0.96 (rank 64 0.61 to 0.96, the full linear prediction 0.63 to 0.96); the linear map explains 0.18 to 0.34 of the weak write's variance on the fitting text; ARC-Easy accuracy moves by -0.30 to -0.04 under zeroing, -0.06 to 0.03 under the per-neuron mean, -0.09 to 0.00 under the oracle sixteen and -0.09 to -0.01 under the predicted sixteen (clean 0.30 to 0.64).

SESSION 159 (2026-10-19, box 11; the user asked for a literature pass and whether the two camps can meet in the middle, then to proceed as I saw fit. The pass (RELATED_WORK s30): Engels et al. 2024 on the linearly predictable half of SAE error, Sun et al. 2025 on dense SAE latents as features, Deng et al. 2026 on a rank-24 dense scaffold beside a sparse code, Pearce et al. 2024 on bilinear MLPs, Knittel and Pfister 2026 on sparse upstream dependencies; the middle: a sparse native drive plus a low-rank field, each camp giving up a claim. Then: the gated remainder of the bypass (e705), the strong field in the reader graph (e706), the brake over OLMo-1B's later checkpoints (e701 late). All pre-registered in results/e705_e706_prereg.json after smokes; 16 jobs through the memory-aware queue with a retry pass. Readings in scripts_writeups/s159_readings.json.)

Over all positions both fields bring the sixteen-wire ratio from 0.83 to 7.00 to 0.26 to 1.45, halving it at five blocks of eight. What remains of a pruned neuron's error, an eighth to a half, is the part of each upstream write outside its block's thirty-two directions..

SESSION 160 (2026-10-19, box 11; the user asked what an entity that looks down on both camps as too human would run, then left the choice to me with the box unconstrained. Six experiments test the model's own criteria against both camps' object-first ones: the read subspace (e707), the thermostat (e708), two clocks (e709), branches (e710), the elasticity test (e711) and the edge program (e712); prior art in RELATED_WORK s31. All pre-registered in results/e707_e712_prereg.json after smokes (one dated revision); 60 jobs through the memory-aware queue with a retry pass. Readings in scripts_writeups/s160_readings.json.)

  - At 6 model-blocks the Fisher information of the output over the next sixty-four tokens gives every vector a read energy; a position's content has nine tenths of its read energy in 5 to 8 directions of widths 768 to 1024; per unit of Euclidean energy, against a random direction's, the content is read at 0.88 to 1.92, the block's strong write at 0.70 to 0.99, its weak write at 0.72 to 1.41, the attention output at 0.68 to 1.32, the OMP rows part at 0.86 to 1.93 and its residual at 1.10 to 1.40; the weak field's sixteen directions are read at 1.23 to 2.51 times a random direction, the strong field's at 0.89 to 2.69 and the stream's sixteen principal directions at 1.76 to 5.89; the Fisher prediction of the KL of removing a part from the state has a Spearman correlation of 0.83 to 0.92 with the measured KL over positions and parts; removing the weak write costs 0.66 to 1.80 times the cost of removing a random vector of its norm; on GPT-2 small a public residual SAE's error is read at 1.38 to 1.53 per unit energy against 1.85 to 2.48 for its reconstruction, holds 0.14 to 0.14 of the content's read energy against 0.15 to 0.19 of its energy, and removing it costs 1.70 to 2.97 times the cost of removing a random vector of its norm.
  - Reading: the model grades a state by a quadratic form, not a subspace: the Fisher information of its output over the next sixty-four tokens predicts the finite KL of removing any part of a position's state at Spearman 0.83 to 0.92, where every subspace cut from the same Fisher failed finite removals in the smokes (LayerNorm couples the parts; see the revisions). Graded per unit of energy, parts are not graded by their energy: GPT-2's sixteen native OMP rows are its most-read part and its own strong write the least, in Pythia and Qwen every part is read at about its energy, the public SAE's error on GPT-2 small holds the same share of the content's read energy as of its Euclidean energy and costs 1.7 to 3 times a random vector of its norm to remove (Gurnee's pathology as read energy: the dark matter is read like the rest), and the fields are read at about twice a random direction, below the pre-registered three, with the stream's leading directions far above. Neither camp's currency is privileged by the output: the rows pass above their energy in GPT-2 only, the dark matter at its energy, the collective field as a second-class citizen..
  - Pre-registered: R1 (the read dimension (nine tenths of the Fisher trace) at mid-depth is under a tenth of the stream's width) confirmed; R2 (the Fisher quadratic form of a part predicts the finite KL of removing it: Spearman at least 0.8 over positions and parts) confirmed; R3 (the weak write's read energy per unit energy is below the strong write's) split (holds for GPT-2 small block 5, not GPT-2 small block 8, GPT-2 medium block 12, Pythia-160m block 6, Pythia-410m block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12); R3b (removing the weak write costs more KL than removing a random vector of its norm) split (holds for GPT-2 small block 8, GPT-2 medium block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12, not GPT-2 small block 5, Pythia-160m block 6, Pythia-410m block 12); R4 (the weak field's sixteen directions carry read energy above three times a random direction's) refuted; R4b (the strong field's do too) refuted; R5 (on GPT-2 small the public SAE's error holds under half as large a share of the content's read energy as of its Euclidean energy) refuted; R5b (and removing it costs more KL than removing a random vector of its norm (Gurnee 2024)) confirmed; R6 (the OMP residual's read energy per unit energy is below the rows part's) split (holds for GPT-2 small block 5, GPT-2 small block 8, GPT-2 medium block 12, not Pythia-160m block 6, Pythia-410m block 12, Qwen2.5-0.5B block 12).

  - At 3 model-blocks the expected gradient of the loss at the perturbed weights (over twenty-four batches of 32 x 1024 tokens) points back toward the original rows with a cosine of 0.10 to 0.14 for sixteen strong rows rotated by forty-five degrees, 0.09 to 0.12 for sixteen alive but weak rows, 0.07 to 0.08 along the original row for sixteen halved rows, and -0.01 to 0.00 for sixteen pairs of neurons swapped whole (an exact symmetry, the noise level), the perturbed rows' gradient being 0.91 to 1.12 times the unperturbed rows' for the rotated strong rows and 0.81 to 0.99 for the weak ones; with every strong row of the block rotated at once (up to 256) the restoring cosine is 0.09 to 0.12 and the rows return by 0.01 to 0.02 in training, the loss recovering by 0.47 to 0.81 free and 0.19 to 0.69 frozen; for the block's weak field swapped into a random subspace the restoring cosine is 0.05 to 0.10 on the whole write matrix and 0.09 to 0.17 on the swapped plane; after 200 to 200 steps of continued training on Pile text at the pre-registered rate the restoring cosine of the rotated strong rows is 0.03 to 0.04, the rows have returned by 0.01 to 0.02 of the way (weak rows 0.01 to 0.02, halved rows recovering 0.01 to 0.01 of their norm) while unperturbed rows keep a cosine of 1.00 to 1.00 to theirs, and the loss lost to the rotations, -0.00 to 0.02 nats, is below the resolution of the recovery measure (the excess over the unperturbed run on the same batches, resolved above 0.003 nats) where defined recovered by n/a with the rows free and n/a with them frozen (weak rows n/a and n/a, halved rows n/a and n/a); the swapped field is restored by its writers by 0.01 to 0.02 and followed by its readers by -0.00 to -0.00, the recomputed field overlapping the original by 0.02 to 0.03 and the swapped subspace by 0.67 to 0.72, with the loss recovered by 0.92 to 1.09 with the writers free and 0.93 to 1.11 frozen.
  - Reading: training defends the function, not the object: on the training distribution the expected gradient at the perturbed point points back toward the original rows with a cosine of 0.09 to 0.14, three to five times the noise floor, the same for sixteen strong rows, sixteen weak rows, all the block's strong rows and the swapped weak field (0.09 to 0.17 on its plane), with a force no larger than an unperturbed row's; the rotations cost 0.0003 to 0.02 nats, and in 200 steps at a realistic rate the rows return by 0.01 to 0.02 while the restoring cosine fades to the floor. The swapped field decides it: a third of a nat, recovered by 0.92 to 1.09 with the writers free and 0.93 to 1.11 with them frozen, while the writers restore the field by 0.02, the readers' energy in the swapped subspace does not move and the recomputed field stays swapped (0.67 to 0.72). The network routes around the displacement in other weights and stops feeling it: a unit survives by what it does, not by where it is..
  - Pre-registered: E0 (the expected gradient at the perturbed point points back toward the original rows: restoring cosine over 0.3 for rotated strong rows) refuted; E0b (the restoring cosine is lower for rotated weak rows than for strong ones) confirmed; E0c (for the swapped field the restoring cosine on the swapped plane is over 0.3) refuted; E0e (rotating every strong row of the block at once (up to 256) gives a restoring cosine over 0.3) refuted; E1 (sixteen strong rows rotated by forty-five degrees return more than halfway (return fraction over 0.5) within 800 steps while unperturbed rows keep a cosine over 0.98 to their originals) refuted; E1e (those rows return by over 0.2 of the way in 200 steps) refuted; E2 (weak rows return less than strong rows by 0.2) refuted; E3 (with the perturbed rows frozen the loss recovers at least half as much as with them free) confirmed; E4 (the swapped field is restored by the writers (writer restoration over 0.5)) refuted; E5 (the readers follow the swapped field by less than 0.1) confirmed; E6 (halved rows recover more than half their norm) refuted.

  | SmolLM2-360M (gated) | 1.325 / 0.300 / 0.555 / 0.534 / 0.546 / 0.616 | 0.77 / 0.58 / 0.60 / 0.59 / 0.54 | 0.42 / 0.33 / 0.24 |

  - In the 4 gated models one linear bypass per branch of the block's open set (sixteen branches found by k-means on a random projection of the gate's sign pattern) recovers 0.59 to 0.66 of the zeroing cost against 0.58 to 0.72 for the single linear bypass and 0.67 to 0.80 for the oracle sixteen, with four branches 0.60 to 0.72 and with sixteen clusters of the normalised input instead of the open set 0.54 to 0.65; in the 2 GELU models the sixteen branches recover 0.76 to 0.94 against 0.73 to 0.93 for the linear bypass; out of domain the sixteen branches recover 0.33 to 0.57 in the gated models against 0.38 to 0.59 for the linear bypass.
  - Reading: the gated remainder is not control flow either: one linear bypass per branch of the open set, sixteen branches found on the gate's sign pattern, recovers no more of the zeroing cost in the gated models than the single linear bypass, four branches do exactly as well as one, sixteen clusters of the input do worse, the branches transfer out of domain no better, and the GELU models gain 0.03. After e705's random quadratic and these branches, what the single linear map misses in a gated block is neither a low-order function of the input nor a branch indexed by the open set or by the input's clusters: it is position-specific in a way the block's own control signal does not index, which leaves it to the attention that wrote the input..
  - Pre-registered: B1 (in the gated models a sixteen-branch mixture closes at least half the gap between the linear bypass and the oracle sixteen) refuted; B2 (in the GELU models it adds under 0.05) confirmed; B3 (the open-set mixture beats the state-clustered mixture of the same size by 0.05) split (holds for OLMo-1B, SmolLM2-360M, not GPT-2 medium, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B); B4 (the mixture keeps 0.7 of its recovery out of domain) split (holds for GPT-2 medium, OLMo-1B, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, not Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-360M); B5 (sixteen branches beat four by 0.03) refuted.

  - Reading: the crowd is not a thermostat: when a block's strong writes are scaled by one and a half, the next three blocks undo a third to three quarters of the injection along its own direction, but the strong writes do the undoing (0.28 to 0.58) and the weak writes a tenth of it (0.06 to 0.13), attention adds nothing, and the response is the same at a half and at double (linear, no brake against excess); the stream's displacement after three blocks is nine tenths of the injection, in other directions. What the later blocks make of it depends on the family: in Pythia, OLMo and Qwen the output KL of the perturbation is six to several hundred times its direct path's (amplification), in GPT-2 medium a third and in SmolLM2-135M a thirtieth (repair). Either way the agent is the strong writes, not the crowd: the crowd's job is the brake off the class (e697), not a loop across depth..

  - At 6 model-blocks, sixteen atoms of rows and fields chosen for a position by pursuit in the blended metric (the output's sampled Fisher at unit mean eigenvalue plus the identity) recover 0.68 to 0.97 of the mean-ablation KL against 0.71 to 0.98 for the Euclidean pursuit, 0.85 to 0.99 for thirty-two Euclidean atoms, 0.46 to 0.92 for the stream's sixteen principal directions and 0.02 to 0.05 for sixteen random atoms; the pure Fisher pursuit recovers -0.19 to 0.47 with a Euclidean residual of 1.62 to 2.06 of the content's energy, the blended one leaves 0.57 to 0.70 of the energy and 0.01 to 0.03 of the read energy against 0.46 to 0.60 and 0.31 to 0.61 for the Euclidean pursuit; rows alone under the blended pursuit recover 0.65 to 0.98 and lambda 0.3 0.52 to 0.95; the field atoms are chosen 0.06 to 0.06 of the time by the Euclidean pursuit and 0.00 to 0.06 by the blended one.
  - Reading: the output's grade does not choose atoms better than energy does: sixteen atoms of rows and fields chosen for a position by pursuit in the blended Fisher metric recover no more of the mean-ablation KL than sixteen chosen in the Euclidean metric (within 0.05 at every block, below it in Pythia-160m), although they leave almost none of the content's read energy where the Euclidean choice leaves a third to a half; the pure Fisher pursuit, fitting the sampled Fisher's range perfectly, recovers less than mean ablation in Pythia and less than half the cost elsewhere, with a reconstruction of twice the content's energy, because the directions the sampled Fisher cannot see are read at finite scale. The field atoms are chosen a sixteenth of the time by either metric, and sixteen Euclidean atoms beat the stream's sixteen principal directions in every model. The lesson is e707's again from the dictionary's side: the Fisher quadratic form grades a given part well (Spearman 0.83 to 0.92) and is not a better objective for choosing parts, since what it misses at first order, the reconstruction's effect through LayerNorm and the later blocks, the Euclidean fit already pays for. The library keeps the blended pursuit as a tool and the Euclidean pursuit as the default..

  - Reading: on the state's own account the SAE wins and the fields do not matter; on the state's response to an intervention the native rows win and the SAE's encoder loses: at GPT-2 small blocks 5 and 8, sixteen atoms replacing a position's state recover 0.92 to 0.95 of the mean-ablation KL from native rows and 0.93 to 0.95 with the upstream fields added, against 0.95 to 0.97 for the SAE encoder's top sixteen latents, 0.97 to 0.98 for sixteen SAE decoder directions chosen by pursuit, 0.97 to 0.99 for rows plus SAE directions and 0.98 to 0.99 for the SAE's full active set of 58 to 82 latents, every dictionary above 0.98 by sixty-four atoms and the stream's sixteen principal directions at 0.84 to 0.89. The fields add 0.01 to the rows on this score, as e703 found for the state's energy and e714 for the pursuit: a field is an atom for a neuron's readers (e706), not for a position's state. The SAE's directions are the better dictionary for this model's state, which they were trained on, by 0.02 to 0.05 at sixteen atoms; but its encoder is a worse selection rule than pursuit over its own directions (0.95 to 0.97 against 0.97 to 0.98 in KL, 0.53 to 0.60 against 0.83 in how the reconstruction responds to a fixed perturbation), and the native rows respond to perturbations more like the state than the encoder's choice does (0.65 to 0.72 against 0.53 to 0.60). The answer to the review's decisive question is therefore split by what is scored: for reconstructing a state's effect, a trained dictionary beats the native rows by a few hundredths and the fields are not the unit; for a neuron's input, the fields are the unit the rows lack (e706, e713)..

  - Reading: at the same number of directions the fields do not beat an SAE's directions at a neuron's firings; they beat them on the suppression itself at small budgets, and both beat random. Beside sixteen wires of GPT-2 small blocks 6 and 9, sixteen field directions chosen on held-out text leave 0.24 and 0.46 of the ablation damage at the firings against 0.23 to 0.31 and 0.41 to 0.42 for sixteen directions of jbloom's L1 and OpenAI's TopK dictionaries and 0.25 and 0.51 for random; at sixty-four, 0.18 and 0.25 against 0.23 to 0.25 and 0.25 to 0.26, random 0.24 and 0.43; at the fields' full dimension (192 and 288), 0.14 and 0.18 against 0.15 to 0.16 and 0.09 to 0.12, random 0.25 and 0.30. Over all positions, where the brake lives, sixty-four field directions leave 0.46 to 0.48 against 0.58 to 0.68 for sixty-four SAE directions, and the fields reproduce the crowd's off-class net sum at a correlation of 0.30 to 0.39 with sixteen directions and 0.52 to 0.60 with sixty-four, against 0.15 to 0.20 and 0.38 for the SAE's directions and 0.12 and 0.23 to 0.27 for random; at the full dimension the two tie (0.66 to 0.67 against 0.65 to 0.72). The SAE's own coefficients on sixteen latents chosen per position (0.13 to 0.27 at the firings) beat every fixed sixteen-direction subspace, with the block's own attention exact in that condition and projected in the others; and the SAE's error projected on the fields improves its full reconstruction at the firings (0.10 to 0.21 to 0.06 to 0.11), as does the projection on random directions by less (to 0.07 to 0.13) and on the SAE's own unused directions by more (to 0.04 to 0.05). Measured at a matched budget, the fields' claim is the brake's: they are the compact carrier of the off-class suppression, not a better dictionary for the firings..

  - Reading: conditional on an SAE's full reconstruction of a state, the fields add nothing to its effect and something to its response. At GPT-2 small blocks 5 and 8 with jbloom's L1 and OpenAI's TopK dictionaries the SAE's full reconstruction recovers 0.976 to 0.989 of the mean-ablation KL; sixteen more atoms chosen by pursuit on what it leaves add 0.002 to 0.006 from the field directions, 0.006 to 0.012 from the native rows, 0.005 to 0.011 from the SAE's own directions and 0.001 to 0.003 from random directions. Under intervention the SAE's reconstruction tracks a fixed perturbation at 0.83 to 0.88 and with sixteen field atoms at 0.93 to 0.97, as high as with sixteen rows (0.91 to 0.97) and higher than with sixteen of the SAE's own directions (0.89 to 0.95) or random atoms (0.85 to 0.89). What the SAE leaves of a state is worth little to the output and something to an intervention, and sixteen field atoms recover that part as well as sixteen native rows do..
  - Pre-registered: N1 (sixteen field atoms add less than 0.02 of the mean-ablation KL to the SAE's full reconstruction in every run) confirmed; N2 (sixteen native rows add at least 0.02 to the SAE's full reconstruction) refuted; N3 (sixteen of the SAE's own directions add at least as much as sixteen field atoms) split (holds for GPT-2 small block 5 with jbloom L1 24k, GPT-2 small block 8 with jbloom L1 24k, GPT-2 small block 8 with OpenAI TopK 32k, not GPT-2 small block 5 with OpenAI TopK 32k); N4 (the intervention fidelity of the SAE plus sixteen field atoms is at least the SAE's own) confirmed.

  - With the final norm applied once (the audit: the recorded readout's KL from the models' own distribution was  nats), keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations costs 0.32 to 8.06 nats across 12 models against 0.24 to 8.68 recorded, and the mean replacement 0.14 to 0.98; the brake's off-class share at the five percent class is 0.40 to 0.88 across 8 model-blocks against 0.52 to 0.88 recorded, sixteen excitatory wires alone cost 4 to 503 times the ablation damage (recorded 6 to 561) and the signed wires 0.89 to 3.04; at the firings the sixteen wires leave 0.37 to 1.97 (recorded 0.41 to 1.95); both fields bring the sixteen wires at the firings to 0.13 to 0.52 across 8 model-blocks (recorded 0.12 to 0.53) against 0.27 to 1.14 for a random subspace; on a state sixteen native rows recover 0.77 to 0.95 and a trained dictionary's top sixteen 0.91 to 0.99 across 8 runs (recorded 0.72 to 0.95 and 0.90 to 0.98).
  - Reading: the record's two broadest claims survive the corrected readout, its weak case gets weaker, and the intervention fidelities of the dictionary comparisons were the numbers the distortion had inflated most. The cost of keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations is 0.32 to 8.06 nats across twelve models against 0.24 to 8.68 recorded, with the mean replacement 0.14 to 0.98 against 0.07 to 2.31: GPT-2 small rises from 0.24 to 2.10 and GPT-2 medium from 0.95 to 3.96, SmolLM2-135M falls from 2.22 to 0.93 and Qwen2.5-7B from 1.57 to 0.32, and OLMo-1B, whose final norm has no gain, does not move. The brake's off-class share is 0.40 to 0.88 against 0.52 to 0.88, unchanged to two decimals at Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2 and down to 0.40 and 0.46 at GPT-2 medium, whose readout the doubling had distorted most; the excitatory runaway is 4 to 503 times the ablation damage (6 to 561 recorded) at every block, the signed wires beat the sixteen by magnitude at the firings in five blocks of eight (six recorded), and the Pile numbers follow the corrected wikitext ones within 0.03. Both fields bring the sixteen wires at the firings to 0.13 to 0.52 (0.12 to 0.53) against 0.27 to 1.14 for a random subspace. On a state the recovered KLs are unchanged, a trained dictionary's top sixteen at 0.91 to 0.99 against 0.77 to 0.95 for sixteen rows, and the fields add 0.00 to 0.01; the intervention fidelities all fall, the rows' from 0.65 to 0.89 to 0.50 to 0.81 and pursuit over OpenAI's directions from 0.34 to 0.49 to 0.06 to 0.30, so the rows' advantage over the L1 encoder under intervention is now one block of two. At a matched budget sixteen field directions leave 0.23 and 0.38 at the firings against 0.30 and 0.33 to 0.36 for sixteen SAE directions and 0.33 and 0.40 for random. The measurement was wrong by a model-dependent amount; the orderings that carried the record's claims mostly survived it, and the ones that did not were the fragile ones, GPT-2 medium's off-class share and the eight-perturbation fidelities..
  - Pre-registered: Q1 (keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations costs at least 0.2 nats in at least 10 of the 12 models) confirmed; Q2 (the mean replacement is cheaper than zeroing in at least 10 of 12) confirmed; Q3 (the corrected cost differs from the recorded one by more than a factor of two in at least 3 of 12 models) confirmed; Q4 (the off-class share of the sixteen-input damage at the five percent class is at least 0.5 in at least 6 of 8 model-blocks) confirmed; Q5 (sixteen excitatory wires alone cost more than three times the ablation damage over all positions in 8 of 8) confirmed; Q6 (sixteen excitatory plus sixteen inhibitory wires cost less at the firings than the sixteen by magnitude in at least 6 of 8) refuted; Q7 (the corrected off-class share is within 0.15 of the recorded one in at least 6 of 8) confirmed; Q8 (both fields bring the sixteen wires' ratio at the firings under 0.5 in at least 6 of 8) confirmed; Q9 (both fields beat a random subspace of their dimension by 0.2 at the firings in at least 4 of 8) confirmed; Q10 (a trained dictionary's top sixteen latents beat sixteen native rows on the recovered KL in all 8 head-to-head runs) confirmed; Q11 (rows plus fields add under 0.03 to the rows in all 8) confirmed; Q12 (at sixteen directions the fields and the SAE's directions are within 0.05 of each other at the firings in 4 of 4) refuted; Q13 (the Pile off-class share is within 0.15 of the corrected wikitext one in 3 of 3) confirmed; Q14 (excitatory wires alone run away (above three times) at k of 8, 16 and 32 in 2 of 2) confirmed; Q15 (the 7B cost is at least 0.2 nats) confirmed; Q16 (the correction moves GPT-2 medium's off-class share more than Pythia-410m's, the readout distortion having been larger there) confirmed.

- e726 On the sparsified MLP of the transcoder paper (the 64 largest neurons per token of a 4B gated model), how much of what the dropped neurons did can a closed-form rank-16 field map put back, against a random map, a trained rank-16 map and the paper's trained d-by-d map, by KL and by the variance left unexplained?:

  | block | top-64 KL (nats) | mean ablation | recovered by the closed-form rank-16 field map [95 percent] | random rank-16 | projection on the field subspace | trained rank-16 | trained full map | FVU: top-64 / field map / trained full |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Qwen3-4B block 24 | 0.050 | 0.151 | 0.332 [0.31, 0.35] | 0.004 | 0.337 | 0.210 [0.18, 0.24] | 0.216 [0.18, 0.25] | 0.56 / 0.37 / 0.45 |
  | Qwen3-4B block 30 | 0.047 | 0.184 | 0.105 [0.08, 0.13] | -0.002 | 0.131 | 0.072 [0.04, 0.10] | 0.090 [0.05, 0.12] | 0.48 / 0.29 / 0.37 |

  - On Qwen3-4B the 64 largest neurons per token leave 0.05 nats of KL at block 24 and block 30 (mean ablation of the block 0.15 to 0.18); of that the closed-form rank-16 field map of the weak write recovers 0.10 to 0.33, a random rank-16 map -0.00 to 0.00, the true weak write projected on the map's subspace 0.13 to 0.34, a trained rank-16 map 0.07 to 0.21 and a trained d-by-d map 0.09 to 0.22; the fraction of the MLP output's variance left unexplained is 0.48 to 0.56 for the 64 neurons alone, 0.29 to 0.37 with the field map and 0.37 to 0.45 with the trained full map.
  - Reading: the premise was wrong by a factor of ten and the comparison still came out in one order. On Qwen3-4B keeping the 64 largest of 9,728 neurons per token leaves 0.050 and 0.047 nats of KL at blocks 24 and 30, not the half nat pre-registered, against 0.151 and 0.184 for replacing the whole block by its mean; a late block of this model is cheap, and its 64 largest neurons per token carry two thirds of what it does. Of the remainder the closed-form rank-16 map of the weak write from the normalised block input recovers 0.332 (0.31 to 0.35) at block 24 and 0.105 (0.08 to 0.13) at block 30, exactly the ceiling of its own output subspace (the true weak write projected on it recovers 0.337 and 0.131), against 0.004 and -0.002 for the same map on a random rank-16 subspace, and above both trained maps at 200 steps: the trained rank-16 map 0.210 and 0.072, the trained d-by-d map on the pruned output 0.216 and 0.090. The variance left unexplained orders the maps the same way (top-64 alone 0.56 and 0.48, with the field map 0.37 and 0.29, with the trained full map 0.46 and 0.37), so the KL and FVU orderings do not differ as predicted. Two of six statements held (random under half of the field map at both blocks; the trained rank-16 map within 0.1 of the closed-form one at block 30 only). The honest limits: the trained maps were still improving when training stopped (the rank-16 loss fell from 0.047 to 0.028 over the 200 steps), so their deficit is a budget statement, not a ceiling; the weak write is 0.48 and 0.38 of the MLP output's energy on held-out text at these blocks, and a rank-16 linear map of it from the block's input explains 0.65 of its variance at block 24 in the fit, so what the map puts back is the linear, low-rank part of the dropped neurons' write, which is most of what a sparsified MLP loses by KL at these two blocks.
  - Pre-registered: B1 (the top-64 neurons alone leave more than 0.5 nats of KL at both blocks) refuted; B2 (the closed-form rank-16 field map recovers at least half of the top-64 KL at both blocks) refuted; B3 (the trained d-by-d map recovers more than the closed-form rank-16 map at both blocks) refuted; B4 (the trained rank-16 map recovers within 0.1 of the closed-form rank-16 map at both blocks) refuted; B5 (the random rank-16 map recovers less than half of what the field map recovers at both blocks) confirmed; B6 (the KL ordering of the trained full map and the field map differs from their FVU ordering at both blocks) refuted.

  - With the controls in the same run: the weakest three quarters of every neuron's activations cost 0.89 to 5.19 nats of KL across 8 models (they carry 0.05 to 0.37 of the activation energy), a count-matched random three quarters 4.09 to 12.35 (0.74 to 0.83 of the energy), and the mass-matched strongest slice 4.65 to 15.20 (0.75 to 0.93 of the energy on 0.10 to 0.39 of the positions); per unit of energy removed the weak slice costs 5.63 to 20.30 nats, the random slice 5.45 to 16.73 and the strong slice 5.70 to 18.64, the weak slice's cost per unit of energy is 0.73 to 2.27 times the random slice's, so the cost of a slice follows the energy it carries to within a factor of about two whichever activations it holds; the top-two probability share at the tokens the weak ablation flips is 0.63 to 0.67 against 0.64 to 0.73 over all tokens; the TinyStories pair on its own text (base loss 1.47 to 1.64 against 9.96 to 10.96 on wikitext): the weakest three quarters cost 1.27 to 4.48 nats (0.17 to 0.37 of the energy), a random three quarters 4.48 to 7.38, the strongest slice 4.24 to 7.82.
  - Reading: the controls that could have killed the cost of the weak activations did not kill it, but they re-size it. A count-matched random three quarters costs 4.09 to 12.35 nats against 0.89 to 3.37 for the weakest three quarters of the six pretrained models, and the mass-matched strongest slice 4.65 to 15.20, so the weakest three quarters are the cheapest three quarters by count, and the cost tracks the energy removed: per unit of energy the three slices cost 5.6 to 20.3, 5.5 to 16.7 and 5.7 to 18.6 nats across the eight runs, the weak slice 0.73 to 2.27 times the random slice (OLMo-1B 2.1 and TinyStories-33M on wikitext 2.3 at the top, Pythia-160m 0.73 at the bottom). The claim that the weak activations matter beyond the energy they carry has no support in these eight models at this measurement; what survives is the plain statement that they carry 5 to 37 percent of the activation energy and cost 0.89 to 5.19 nats when removed, with a cost per unit of energy within a factor of about two of any other slice. The tokens whose top prediction flips under the weak ablation have a lower top-two share than the run of tokens (0.63 to 0.67 against 0.64 to 0.73), the predicted direction with a gap of 0.01 to 0.09. The TinyStories prediction failed twice: measured on wikitext the two models are out of their distribution (base loss 10 to 11 nats), and measured on their own text (base loss 1.5 to 1.6) their weakest three quarters cost 1.27 and 4.48 nats, the random three quarters 4.48 and 7.38 and the strongest slice 4.24 and 7.82, the pattern of the pretrained models at the same cost per unit of energy (7.4 and 12.0 against 6.0 and 9.8 for the random slice). A children's-story model with a tiny vocabulary keeps its weak activations as costly as GPT-2 does, so the cost is not a product of broad pretraining.
  - Pre-registered: X1 (the mass-matched strong slice costs more KL than the weakest three quarters in every model) confirmed; X2 (the weakest three quarters cost at least 0.2 nats in every pretrained model and in neither TinyStories model) refuted; X3 (a random three quarters costs more than the weakest three quarters in every model) confirmed; X4 (the tokens whose top prediction flips under the weak ablation have a lower top-two share than the median token, in every model) confirmed.
