  - On Qwen3.5-4B the zoo's 0.8-residual-norm dose is 5 to 86 times the row's own q999 activation across the nine zoo rows (Meowscow 5, Heavy 86); the nine rows sit at global R_dir percentiles 0.22 to 0.86 and R_nat percentiles 0.15 to 1.00; at the zoo's dose the personas hit their regex on 0.10 to 1.00 of ten held-out prompts (the evil pair 0.50 at its own dose 1.0) while the random rows of the same layers hit 0.00 to 0.10; at 3 x q999 the hit rates are 0.00 to 0.10 and at 10 x 0.00 to 0.60; the zoo rows cost 0.37 to 3.77 nats of KL on the model's own answers at 0.8 against 0.31 to 1.04 for the random rows; the two known landmines sit at global R_dir percentiles 0.66 and 0.49 (within their layers 0.93 and 0.40); the top-8 rows by R_dir cost a median +1.52 nats of held-out NLL at 0.8 against +0.40 for random rows and +0.73 for the bottom rows; the first-order ablation proxy has Spearman 0.88 with the measured mean-ablation KL over 24 rows; before the blind judge the WDD-chosen rows at 3 x q999 reach consistency 2 on 2 of 10 against 0 of 10 random rows, each layer's top-R_dir row at the zoo's 0.8 on 0 of 10 against 2 of 10, and the twenty random rows at 0.8 on 4 of 20.
  - Reading: the zoo and WDD rank rows by different things, and the run says which is which. By the sampled-Fisher read energy of all 294,912 write rows of Qwen3.5-4B, measured from the model's own logits on natural text, the zoo's 43 cards are ordinary rows: global R_dir percentiles 0.08 to 0.89 (median 0.57, none in the top tenth; within their layers 0.07 to 0.98), R_nat percentiles 0.01 to 1.00; the two known landmines sit at 0.66 and 0.49. What the zoo steers is a direction at a dose far outside the row's own range: 0.8 residual norms is 5 to 119 times the row's 99.9th-percentile activation over the cards (median 28; 5 to 86 over the nine validated rows, Meowscow the one below 10). The personas appear between 0.4 and 0.8 residual norms (six of seven at hit rate 0.7 or more at 0.8; the evil pair 0.3 at 0.8 and 0.5 at 1.0, under the pre-registered 0.6) and nowhere at 1 or 3 times the row's own amplitude (hit rate at most 0.1; at 10 times Meowscow alone reaches 0.6; at 30 times, which is 0.3 to 0.6 residual norms, six of seven), while random rows of the same layer and sign hit at most 0.1 at every dose. The zoo's rows are the expensive directions, not the cheap ones: 0.37 to 3.77 nats of KL on the model's own answers at 0.8 (median 1.55) against 0.31 to 1.09 (median 0.58) for the random rows. A blind judge (97 shuffled sets of six answers, key withheld) was calibrated by the zoo itself, giving seven of eight steers consistency 2 (Meowscow 0), none of their random controls and not the base model; it then gave a nameable theme to 4 of 20 random rows at the zoo's dose (bookbinding, finger-to-nose tests, cold refusals, an emotional loop) and a partial one to 7 more, so an overdriven direction is a persona about one time in five, under the pre-registered bar of 6 in 20. WDD's own choices carry no persona: the top-R_nat row of each layer is a massive-activation row (q999 4.7 to 187 against a typical 0.4), silent at the zoo's 0.8 (median KL 0.16) and destructive at 3 times its own amplitude (median 3.9 nats, 7 of 10 degenerate before the judge, 2 of 10 with a theme), where random rows at 3 times their amplitude do nothing (KL at most 0.03, 0 of 10 changed); the readers' favourite row of each middle layer at 0.8 gets 0 of 10 and costs less than a random row of its layer (median 0.57 against 0.73 nats). The global top-8 rows by R_dir per unit norm (layers 0 to 2) cost +1.52 nats of held-out NLL at 0.8 against +0.40 for random rows, but the bottom-8, all in layer 31, cost +0.73, because the zoo's dose is in units of each layer's residual norm (2.5 at layer 0, 52.7 at layer 31) and R_dir per unit norm is not the predicted cost at that dose; the dose-scaled predictor was not pre-registered. The ablation proxy is sound (Spearman 0.88 over 24 rows). Three of twelve statements held.

  - Reading: the dose-scaled predictor is dead, and it dies the way the pre-registration's own arithmetic said it would. Scaling the read energy per unit norm by the squared dose makes it a worse predictor of the cost at 0.8 residual norms than the unscaled energy: Spearman 0.30 against 0.35 with the held-out NLL cost over the 24 stage-1 rows, 0.11 against 0.33 over the 40 stage-3 rows, 0.15 against 0.43 over the 78 pooled rows, and the unscaled energy is itself weak (0.43, and 0.41 once the extreme stage-1 groups are removed). The failure is structural: the measured cost at the zoo's dose falls with depth (Spearman -0.49 with the layer over the pooled rows, -0.56 in stage 1) while the squared dose rises 450 times from layer 0 to layer 31 and the median read energy falls 1,500 times, so P is U-shaped in depth (1.0 nats at layer 0, 0.11 at layers 7 to 16, 0.29 at layer 31) and the bottom-8 rows of layer 31, which cost 0.73 nats of held-out NLL, get the smallest P of any group (0.044 against 0.15 for the random rows and 16.7 for the top-8). P overpredicts the early rows by an order of magnitude (10.9 times the measured KL for the top-8) and underpredicts the late rows by one (0.11 for the bottom-8); 6 of 24 rows land within a factor of three. Within a layer P ranks exactly as R_dir, so it leaves the landmines where R_dir left them in their layers (percentiles 0.93 and 0.40) and drops them globally (0.36 and 0.11 against 0.66 and 0.49), and the 43 cards stay ordinary (P percentiles 0.11 to 0.88, median 0.46, none in the top tenth). The pairs say the same: the WDD-chosen row has the larger P in 18 of 20 layer-matched pairs and the larger measured KL in 7, and the zoo's rows beat their controls in 4 of 8 specs by P and 7 of 8 by KL. A second-order expansion in the injected norm does not describe a perturbation of 0.8 residual norms; the quadratic form of the model's own logits predicts removals and small injections (e707, e728's ablation proxy at 0.88) and stops there. A landmine predictor at the zoo's dose has to be measured at the dose (e729).
  - Pre-registered: D1 (Over the 24 stage-1 rows, the Spearman correlation of P with the held-out NLL cost at the zoo's 0.8 is at least 0.5; p 0.35) refuted; D2 (The dose scaling repairs the inverted bottom group: the median P of the bottom-8 rows exceeds the median P of the random-8 rows; p 0.1) refuted; D3 (Calibration: for at least 12 of the 24 stage-1 rows, P is within a factor of 3 of the measured KL on the model's own answers at the zoo's 0.8; p 0.4) refuted; D4 (Over the 40 stage-3 and stage-3b rows at the zoo's 0.8, the Spearman correlation of P with the KL on the model's own answers is at least 0.5; p 0.15) refuted; D5 (For at least 6 of the 8 stage-2 specs, the P of the zoo's rows (summed over a spec's rows) exceeds the P of its same-layer, same-sign random controls; p 0.25) refuted; D6 (At least one of the two known landmines (L13 N142, L15 N143) is in the global top 10 percent of P over all 294,912 rows; p 0.15) refuted.

  - Reading: the direct-path vocabulary is a generation-free readout of what an overdriven row will say when its effect is a vocabulary, and a selector of word-spammers when used as a finder. From the weights alone, one matrix product per row, it retrieves six of the nine zoo rows inside the top 1 percent of 589,824 (row, sign) candidates by the mass on each card's own regex, including the layer-4 and layer-5 rows the pre-registration expected to fail (the pair's two rows and the layer-5 Galactic row are the misses). For rows no one chose by hand it says what the steer will say: over e728's forty judged rows the token-list judge gives a clear theme to all four rows whose generations had one and to none of the 23 whose generations had none (Spearman 0.79 over the twenty random rows), and a second blind judge matches 7 of its 11 themes to the generation judge's and none of 11 shuffled pairs. What it does not do is find the zoo: the cards' lists read as themed no more often than random rows' (12 of 43 against 11 of 43), their concentration is ordinary (AUC 0.66), and the pair's rows are not retrieved, so most hand-found personas are made downstream of the row, not in its direct path. As a finder it selects loops: the twenty most concentrated rows (N_eff 2 after the single-token spikes are excluded) get consistency 2 from the generation judge on 19 of 20 against 9 of 20 for their same-layer random controls, but 12 of 20 are degenerate (controls 3 of 20) and cost a median 1.26 nats against 0.41, and with the loops excluded they carry a theme on 7 of 20 against 6 of 20; the lookup's best row for each regex hits its words at raw rates that pass the bars (6 of 8 within 0.2 of the card's, 5 of 8 at least half) and loops on them in 5 of 8 cases, with one clean retrieval (the Hugs regex: 10 of 10 non-degenerate answers on theme at 1.14 nats against the card's 2.46) and one partial (Galactic). Seven of ten statements held, three of them (B1, C1, C2) on looping outputs the bars did not exclude; B3, written for that, failed. A finder from the weights needs the dose as a second knob, since a row whose direct path is one or two words loops at 0.8 residual norms, and the themes made downstream need the vocabulary measured at the dose (e731), not the direct path (e730).

The row whose direct path says the 'wen' of the model's name, suppressed at layer 27, renames the model Q3 in 20 of 20 answers and makes 14 of them say Baidu, fully coherent at 0.31 nats (0.11 nats at the smoke's lower dose, same flip); the row whose direct path is the end-of-turn token cuts answers from 364 tokens to 11 at one sign (15 of 20 non-degenerate, the rest one-line) and runs all 20 to the cap at the other (the base has 15 of 20 there, which is why the lengthening bar, set at 1.4 times the base, could not be met). The rows found for Chinese, capitals, markdown and the think token all do what their token says and then loop on it: the Chinese row fills 80 percent of the characters with a two-character phrase (19 of 20 answers loop by a character check the word-level check missed, so S3 is a hollow hold), the capitals row shouts a readable sentence (9 of 20 answers both shouting and clean over their first 40 words) before looping, the markdown row at its suppressing sign removes a third of the bold markers and at its pushing sign emits 392 asterisks, the think row emits only think tags. No row says the smiley. At 4 and 8 nats of direct-path shift the last-layer rows move nothing (KL 0.005 to 0.08), at 16 the one-token rows spam, so the direct path cannot dose a row whose vocabulary is one token; by the pivot rule the dose has to be measured, not read. The segues carry the session. A persona survives its own injection: with the zoo's 0.8 on the prompt and one generated token only, 4 of 6 zoo rows keep their theme at half the all-token rate or better (Galactic 9 of 10, Vegas 7 of 10), and with 16 tokens all six do; read back on its own all-token answers with no injection, each row fires at 5 to 22 times its level on the base answers and at 0.5 to 1.8 times its natural maximum, so the write side of the atom feeds its read side through the text it wrote. Two rows at once: Jesus silences 4 of 5 partners, Vegas silences Galactic, and Heavy, a word-theme, blends with 4 of 5 (both themes in 6 to 9 of 10 answers), 12 of 15 pairs intact. The word's own output direction, dosed by the same rule, matches the row for heavy (10 of 10 at 0.39 nats against the row's 0.84) and beats it for cat (5 of 10 at 0.11 against 1 of 10 at 0.45) and reaches 1 to 4 of 10 for the four persona themes against the rows' 7 to 10: the vocabulary is the library for words and the rows are the library for personas, as session 168 read it. Zeroing the fifty rows with the largest R_nat costs 0.015 nats, fifty random rows 0.001: no such fifty hold the model up (e731).
